In the first experiment, students were put in a plain room without phones, books, or anything to write with, and told to think for 6 to 15 minutes. They had to stay seated and awake. The students said they didn’t enjoy the experience and found it hard to concentrate. Even thinking about what to think about didn’t help.

The experiment was repeated at people’s homes, and the results were similar. People found it even more unpleasant and often broke the rules by getting up or using their phones.

The researchers also tested over 100 people, aged 18 to 77, from a church and a farmers’ market, and they also disliked being left with their thoughts.

Organic food contains more antioxidants – substances linked to good health – and fewer toxic metals and pesticides than traditionally grown food, according to a large scientific study. Researchers suggest that eating organic fruits and vegetables could have similar benefits to eating one or two extra portions of the recommended ‘five a day’.

The study, led by Professor Carlo Leifert at Newcastle University, found that organic food had significantly higher levels of antioxidants, between 19% and 69% more. This is the first study to clearly show differences between organic and conventionally grown fruits, vegetables, and cereals. 

The researchers believe this increase in antioxidants could be important for health, as antioxidants have been linked to a lower risk of serious illnesses like heart disease and cancer. They analysed 343 previous studies from around the world to reach these conclusions.

However, some experts disagree with the findings. Professor Tom Sanders from King’s College London believes the differences may be small and not significant. He also pointed out that organic cereals contain less protein. 

The Soil Association, which supports organic farming, welcomes the research, stating it proves that farming methods affect food quality. Plants naturally produce antioxidants to protect themselves, and organic crops may have more because they aren’t protected by chemical sprays. Other factors, like the type of plant grown and the use of natural fertilizers, may also play a role.

The study also found higher levels of the toxic metal cadmium and four times more pesticide residue in conventionally grown crops. While these levels were still within legal limits, researchers suggest that cadmium can build up in the body over time.

Some critics argue that the large number of studies included could affect the results, or that differences are due to factors like soil type and climate.

Emmanuel Limal, a 43-year-old actor, was tired of dating women who didn’t want to have children, or didn’t say if they did. He lived in Copenhagen, Denmark, and had been looking for a partner to start a family with for 20 years. He tried online dating, but was disappointed.

He noticed many women presented themselves as very busy with travel and hobbies, but didn’t mention wanting children. Some profiles said they might want kids “someday,” but their lifestyles suggested they wouldn’t have time. Limal already has a six-year-old daughter, and comes from a large family – his father has eleven siblings – so he wants more children. He found it difficult to talk about wanting a family when meeting new people, as he thought it was a sensitive topic.

Then he found a profile of a 38-year-old woman who honestly said she wanted children, even though she thought it was unusual to admit. This inspired him to create a dating website called Babyklar.nu, which means ‘baby-ready now’ in English.

The website is like other dating sites, but asks people to be honest about wanting to start a family soon. It also asks if they are happy to date someone who already has children. Limal didn’t want to ask people exactly how many children they wanted, as he thought that would be too impersonal.

The website became very popular quickly, with 50 people signing up every hour after it launched. He has already heard from couples who met on the site and are now in relationships, and expects the first baby born through the site to arrive next summer. More men (53%)

The New York City subway system is full of tiny living things, like bacteria. Scientists have now started to study and map these bacteria to understand what lives underground.

Dr. Christopher Mason and his team spent 18 months collecting samples from turnstiles, seats, and stations. They found over 15,000 different types of bacteria, almost half of which were bacteria. They even found traces of bacteria that cause diseases like meningitis, anthrax, and bubonic plague.

However, the scientists say there is no need to worry. The amount of dangerous bacteria was very small, and no one has been sick from these diseases in New York for many years. Most of the bacteria they found are harmless or even helpful – they help break down waste, just like the bacteria in our bodies help us digest food.

The types of bacteria found also showed what people were eating. They found bacteria from cheese, pizza, kimchi, and sauerkraut. They even found cucumber DNA! Bacteria that can cause diarrhea, skin infections, and urinary tract infections were also common.

The scientists found more bacteria in busy stations like Times Square and Grand Central. They also found that the Bronx had the most diverse types of bacteria, while Staten Island had the fewest. Interestingly, they found bacteria from the ocean near South Ferry station, and some were even from Antarctica!

The researchers believe these bacteria are a normal part of city life and may even be important for a healthy environment. They hope this research will help health officials understand and track diseases in the future. 

Dr. Mason says people should still wash their hands, get enough sleep, and eat healthy food. He feels even more confident riding the subway after learning about the bacteria that live there

Nelson Mandela, a key figure in the fight for freedom in Africa and a hero to many people worldwide, has died at the age of 95.

South Africa’s first black president died at his home in Johannesburg, surrounded by his family, after being unwell for some time. The current president, Jacob Zuma, announced the news on television, saying Mandela had “died peacefully” at 8.50pm. 

Zuma said the country was very sad to lose “its greatest son,” and that Mandela showed people what they could be. He added that Mandela helped bring South Africans together and they would say goodbye to him together. Zuma announced a state funeral and ordered flags to be lowered to half-mast.

Archbishop Desmond Tutu led a memorial service, saying South Africa should be like Mandela as a person. Barack Obama, the US president, called Mandela “Madiba” – his clan name – and said he changed South Africa with his strength and willingness to sacrifice his freedom for others. Obama said Mandela’s life showed that people and countries can improve. He also praised Mandela for giving up power and forgiving those who put him in prison, setting a good example for everyone.

David Cameron, the UK prime minister, said Mandela was a “hero of our time” and that a “great light has gone out in the world.” FW de Klerk, the South African president who freed Mandela and won the Nobel Peace Prize with him, said the news was very sad for South Africa and the world. He described Mandela as someone who brought people together.

People in South Africa gathered in the streets to remember Mandela’s life. In Soweto, they sang and danced near his old house, singing

Brazil saw some of its largest protests in many years, with over 100,000 people demonstrating across the country. People were unhappy with strong police actions, poor public services, and the high costs of hosting the World Cup.

The main protests happened in cities like Rio de Janeiro, São Paulo, and Brasilia. They began peacefully, but some turned violent with clashes between protesters and police. Some people attacked cars and buses.

These protests started after smaller demonstrations against increased bus fares. Protesters said police used too much force, including rubber bullets and tear gas. The recent protests grew quickly, with people expressing anger about rising costs, poor quality of services like healthcare, and concerns about inequality and corruption.

In Rio, police were injured and property was damaged. Protesters wrote slogans like “Revolution” and messages against the mayor and governor. One protester was seriously injured.

People protested for many reasons. Some were angry with the government, while others were concerned about unemployment and education. In Brasilia, protesters even entered the area around the national congress building. There were also clashes near a football stadium in Belo Horizonte.

In São Paulo, where there had been previous clashes, large crowds gathered again, but the protests were mostly peaceful. Many protesters said they learned about the protests through social media, with some carrying signs saying “We come from Facebook”.

Many of the protesters were young people who had never participated in a large demonstration before. They felt that Brazil was facing a crisis with rising prices and that it was time to react.

The protests were compared to similar events in Turkey and other countries. Some protesters wore masks used by protest groups like Anonymous.

The protests were nicknamed the “vinegar revolution

Amsterdam still seems open and tolerant to visitors. The city’s mayor recently said that coffee shops selling marijuana will remain open, even with a new national law trying to reduce drug tourism. However, Amsterdam might lose its tolerant image because of plans to move people who cause trouble to temporary homes made from shipping containers.

Mayor Eberhard van der Laan says this new policy, costing £810,000, is to protect people from abuse and harassment. These temporary homes have been called “scum villages” because a politician from a far-right party suggested sending “repeat offenders” to a similar place last year.

A spokesperson for the Mayor, Bartho Boer, says the plans are not unfair. He explains that Amsterdam wants to protect its values of freedom and tolerance for everyone, including gay and lesbian people and those who are harassed. Boer says these “villages” are for people who are very violent and repeatedly harass others, not for minor neighbour disputes.

People who cause “extreme trouble” will be evicted from their homes and moved to these simple container homes in industrial areas of the city. Boer says these containers have showers and kitchens and were previously used for students. He explains that the city doesn’t want to reward bad behaviour by giving these people better housing.

A newspaper in the Netherlands noted that in the 1800s, troublemakers were moved to villages that quickly became poor areas. However, Boer says the city has learned from this mistake and will not house these people together. He says it’s more accurate to call them “scum houses” because only one family will be placed in each area.

Men in management positions receive bonuses that are double the amount given to women doing the same job. Over a lifetime, this means men earn £141,500 more in bonuses than women.

In 2012, the Chartered Management Institute (CMI) found that men in UK management roles received an average bonus of £6,442, while women received £3,029. For top-level directors, men received £63,700 in bonuses compared to £36,270 for women in the last year.

These figures show that there is unfairness in how men and women are paid in British businesses. The CMI believes companies need to change how they manage people, allowing more flexibility and focusing on results, not just time spent at work. They also want more openness about how performance and pay are decided. They believe this would improve both company performance and employee well-being.

Researchers say bonuses are often decided without clear rules, and should be more transparent. While some argue that women may choose jobs with fewer bonuses, the difference in bonus amounts is making the overall pay gap worse. The government says the pay gap is getting smaller, but men still earn 10% more than women on average.

Maria Miller, the Minister for Women and Equalities, said the CMI’s findings prove women are still at a disadvantage in the workplace. The government is trying to address this by making it illegal to keep pay secret, giving legal powers to investigate unfair pay, and encouraging companies to improve how they hire, promote, and pay women through the “Think, Act, Report” scheme. They have also introduced shared parental leave and flexible working options.

Maria was sitting in a community centre on a cold Tuesday afternoon. She was waiting for her number, 34, to be called. When her turn came, she received a brown paper bag with food like pasta, eggs, and cornflakes. She could also choose between butternut squash and carrots.

Maria is one of over 400 families who visit the East Hampton Food Pantry each week. The food pantry helps people with food during the winter months. East Hampton is a place where many rich and famous people have homes, but it also has a community of people who struggle to live there.

Maria works long hours cleaning houses during the summer, but she doesn’t find work in the winter. “The people who come here are rich, but we who live here are not,” she says. Many people share small rooms because they can’t afford the rent. Some families with five children live in basements and still pay over $1,000 a month.

Vicki Littman, who leads the food pantry, says more and more people need help. In 2015, they gave out over 31,000 food parcels. She explains that when the summer season ends, people’s working hours are reduced, and more families need their help. The food they provide lasts for two or three days.

Littman says it’s surprising to some people that there is poverty in a place known for its wealth. She says people often see the glamorous side of the Hamptons – parties, beaches, and expensive houses – but they don’t see the workers who keep everything running. These workers, like gardeners and waitresses, depend on summer income to survive the winter

Robert Mysłajek, a scientist, was excited to find wolf droppings on a mountain path. Seeing wolf poo is a good sign, because wolves are rare in Poland. However, their numbers are increasing – now around 1,500, double the amount from 15 years ago. Wolves, along with bears and lynx, are among the last large predators in Europe.

Scientists from other countries are coming to Poland to learn how it has protected wolves, despite old stories that portrayed them negatively. By examining the droppings, Mysłajek can learn about a wolf’s diet, sex, age, health, and family. He discovered one wolf had eaten a deer. 

DNA tests show Polish wolves travel long distances. One wolf even reached the Netherlands before being hit by a car. A wolf pack needs a large area – about 250 square kilometers – to live and hunt.

A group of students from the UK visited Poland to study wolves. They discussed whether wolves could be reintroduced to Scotland, where they haven’t lived since the 18th century. 

Mysłajek explained that Poland has a different situation than Scotland. Poland eats more pork and has fewer sheep. However, both countries have large deer populations and a problem with too many wild boar, which damage crops. Wolves can help control these animal numbers.

Wolves are strong animals and can travel up to 30 kilometers during a hunt. A pack usually has 8-9 members, and only one pair has cubs each year. The whole group helps care for the young.

It’s a good time to be at the World Cup in Brazil, according to England fan Anthony McDowell. He was enjoying the sunshine on Copacabana beach, walking to a match. McDowell said the country is beautiful, the people are friendly, and there’s a great atmosphere. He hopes the England team will play well.

Many fans from around the world are enjoying a party on the beach, with national flags and songs. They are waiting for games to start on a large screen at FanFest. There were so many people, it was like when the Pope visited.

This happy mood is different from the problems with protests, transport, and stadiums before the tournament began. Now that the games have started, fans want to have a good time. Brian Hill, a fan from Sunderland, said he almost didn’t come because of the cost and difficulty of travelling. But now he’s here, he’s enjoying it.

The trip hasn’t been perfect. Hill travelled for over 20 hours and was delayed getting from the airport. His son had his sunglasses stolen on the beach. They were also surprised that not many bars had big screens to watch the games. But, like other fans, they love the atmosphere.

The football has been exciting, with lots of goals – 28 in the first eight games, much more than in 2010. The Netherlands’ Robin van Persie scored a fantastic goal, and Latin American teams have been winning their games.

So far, the tournament hasn’t had major problems, although it’s not been trouble-free. The stadiums were built late, but they seem safe.

There have been some empty seats at matches.

In the UK, a girl born today can expect to live to around 82 years old, while a boy can expect to live to 78. People in Andorra live even longer, to 85 and 79 years old respectively. Life expectancy in the US is slightly lower, at 81 and 76. However, in the Central African Republic, people live much shorter lives, averaging 49 and 44 years.

Generally, lifespans are increasing worldwide. Fewer young children are dying than they did 40 years ago. In 1970, 16.4 million children under five died, but in 2010, this number fell to 6.8 million – a decrease of almost 60%.

To understand these changes, a research group called the Institute of Health Metrics and Evaluation (IHME) in Seattle studied global health for five years, with the help of nearly 500 researchers. By knowing how and why people die, the world can work to improve healthcare. 

The IHME published seven studies in The Lancet medical journal. Their methods are sometimes different from traditional approaches. For example, when official records are unavailable, they interview families to understand how someone died. One surprising finding was that around 1.2 million people die from malaria each year – double the previously believed number. They found that malaria affects more adults than previously thought, as adults in Africa are often diagnosed with the disease in hospitals.

While the World Health Organization (WHO) welcomed the IHME study, some scientists there are being careful about accepting the new numbers until they see more evidence. However, they agree that the IHME’s research

In the town of Rjukan, Norway, there’s a statue of Sam Eyde, the man who founded the town and built its factories. The statue looks towards a steep mountainside. Behind the statue is Gaustatoppen, an 1,800-metre mountain. Rjukan is in a narrow valley and was built for the workers at Eyde’s factories.

Eyde used the Rjukanfossen waterfall to create hydroelectric power, making it the world’s biggest power plant at the time. However, the mountains around Rjukan block the sun for half the year. From late September to mid-March, the town of 3,400 people doesn’t get much sunlight.

Recently, something surprising happened. Three large mirrors, powered by the sun, were placed high on the mountain. These mirrors follow the sun and reflect its light down onto the town square, bringing bright sunlight to Rjukan.

People are amazed. Ingrid Sparbo, a retired woman who has lived in Rjukan all her life, says the light is “warming, not just physically, but mentally.” Families are enjoying the sunlight, and people are taking photos.

Eivind Toreid, an engineer, thinks the light is almost like real sunlight, like a spotlight. Heidi Fieldheim heard about the mirrors on the radio and says they have brought more happiness than she expected.

The idea came from Martin Andersen, an artist who moved to Rjukan in 2001. He noticed the town was in shadow and wanted to find a way to bring sunlight to the square. After twelve years, he worked with a company to install the three large glass mirrors.

Four minutes of exercise sounds short, but Dr. Izumi Tabata’s training method is very challenging. It involves 20 seconds of intense effort, followed by 10 seconds of rest, repeated eight times. People often feel exhausted during the workout!

Dr. Tabata first tested this method on his university students in the early 1990s. They were very tired after just four minutes, but after six weeks, they saw improvements in their fitness. He and coach Irisawa Koichi had noticed that short bursts of hard exercise were as good as longer, easier workouts when training Japan’s speed skating team.

Dr. Tabata wanted to prove this with an experiment. He divided students into two groups. One group did one hour of cycling at a normal pace five times a week. The other group warmed up for ten minutes, then did four minutes of Tabata intervals four times a week, plus one 30-minute cycling session with some intervals.

After six weeks, the Tabata group improved their anaerobic capacity by 28% and their VO2 max (a measure of fitness) by 15%. They only exercised for 88 minutes a week! The other group also improved their VO2 max, but only by 10%, and didn’t improve their anaerobic capacity. Dr. Tabata also found that people’s hearts grew stronger after just three weeks. Research also suggests it may lower the risk of diabetes.

However, this workout isn’t easy. You need to push yourself to the limit on a bike, rowing machine, or with exercises like sprints. It should feel very difficult, especially towards the end. Dr. Tabata says you should be

In 2005, BlackBerry became popular when it introduced instant messaging on mobile phones. At that time, the iPhone didn’t exist yet, and BlackBerry was a major Canadian export.

Six years later, in 2011, during riots in London and other English cities, BlackBerry Messenger (BBM) was very effective at helping people coordinate. Politicians even suggested temporarily stopping the service. However, by 2013, people were losing interest in BlackBerry phones, and BBM was becoming less popular. Many new messaging apps appeared, like those from Facebook and Apple, as well as WhatsApp and Kik. These apps were free and worked on most phones, allowing users to send texts, photos, voice messages, and videos.

BlackBerry tried to compete by releasing BBM for Android and Apple phones. Over 20 million people downloaded it, but many experts believe this wasn’t enough to save the service. James Gooderson, an 18-year-old technology blogger, said it was too late, as WhatsApp had already become the preferred app for young people. BBM had 80 million users, but WhatsApp had 300 million. BBM also lacked features found in other apps, such as video calls (like Skype) or location sharing (like Path).

The way people communicate is changing, with more focus on images and videos. Apps like Instagram and Snapchat are popular. BBM was once very powerful – it was even credited with helping start a revolution in Egypt and providing faster news during the London riots. A disagreement has started between countries over whether people in Bolivia should be allowed to chew coca leaves. Coca leaves are the main ingredient in cocaine. Bolivia wants to be allowed to continue this traditional practice for its indigenous people, and has asked for a special exception to a 1961 agreement about drugs.

Bolivia says its 2009 constitution protects coca as part of its culture, and that the leaf itself is not harmful. For centuries, people in South America have chewed coca leaves for energy and medicinal purposes. Some groups support Bolivia, saying it is defending the rights of its people.

However, the UN’s International Narcotics Control Board (INCB), which checks countries follow drug rules, believes Bolivia’s request could damage international efforts to control drugs. Countries like the UK, US, Italy, and Russia also disagree with Bolivia. They worry that allowing coca chewing could lead to more cocaine production.

The UK recognizes the cultural importance of coca leaves, but fears it could increase the illegal cocaine trade. Bolivia was originally told to ban coca chewing in 1964, but was given 25 years to do so. This period ended in 1989, and the issue has been debated ever since.

In 2011, Bolivia said it was leaving the 1961 agreement. Recently, it rejoined, but asked for an exception to the rule about coca chewing. This is the first time a country has asked for such a change to the agreement. Russia fears this will increase illegal cocaine and set a bad example for other countries.

A committee in the British parliament has suggested the UK support Bolivia, arguing it’s important for countries to stay within the agreement. Bolivia

Before he died, Carl Sagan recorded a message for future Mars explorers, saying he would be happy for them and wished he could join them. Now, seventeen years after Sagan shared his vision in 1996, a company in the Netherlands called Mars One is planning to make that vision real. They want to send four astronauts to Mars in 2023 to start a human colony. However, there are some difficulties.

Living on Mars would be hard on the astronauts’ bodies. The gravity on Mars is only 38% of Earth’s, which could seriously affect their bones, muscles, and heart. More importantly, the trip is one-way – there is no plan to bring the astronauts back to Earth. The Mars One website says a return trip is not possible with current technology. They would need a rocket with enough fuel to leave Mars, life support for a seven-month journey, and a way to land safely back on Earth.

Despite these challenges, Mars One says it has already received 10,000 applications. The applicants are between 18 and 62 years old, and mostly men. One applicant, a 32-year-old American woman named Cynthia, said she dreamed of going to Mars since she met Carl Sagan at a lecture when she was a child. He asked her if she would travel in a spaceship for two years, and she said yes. She now sees the Mars One project as a chance to make her dream come true.

Scientists have revealed new information about the death and burial of King Richard III. At a press conference at Leicester University, they announced they are certain they have found his remains. 

The king’s body was discovered in a car park in Leicester. Researchers confirmed his identity using DNA tests and by studying his bones, which showed he had a curved spine called scoliosis. The bones were found in a small grave at Grey Friars church.

Philippa Langley, from the Richard III Society, led the search for the king’s body for many years. She secured funding for the project despite many people doubting it would succeed. A new tomb for Richard III is being designed for Leicester Cathedral, and a ceremony to bury him there will likely take place next year. A visitor centre is also planned near the excavation site.

Researchers showed how Richard III died in battle at Bosworth on August 22, 1485. He was the last English king to die in battle. They found evidence of a severe blow to the back of his skull, likely from a halberd – a medieval weapon with a sharp axe blade. This blow would have killed him instantly. 

Other injuries suggest his body was badly treated after his death. He was likely stripped, mocked, and wounded with knives while being carried back to Leicester. One wound to his buttock could only have happened after he was dead and no longer wearing armour. This supports stories that his naked body was displayed on a horse.

Scientists have experimented with mice to understand how false memories are created. This is important because people sometimes falsely ‘remember’ things that didn’t happen, which can cause problems in court cases where witnesses give evidence. Sometimes, people are wrongly convicted because of incorrect witness statements, but later proven innocent with other evidence like DNA.

To study this, researchers at MIT, led by Susumu Tonagawa, changed memories in mice by controlling individual brain cells. Memories are created when the brain records details about experiences – things, places, and times – as physical and chemical changes in brain cells called ‘engrams’. 

Tonagawa’s team found that both real and false memories use the same parts of the brain. They used a technique called optogenetics, which lets them control brain cells with light. They changed cells in the mouse’s hippocampus – a part of the brain important for memory – so they would react when exposed to blue light.

In the experiment, mice first explored a room. Then, they were placed in a different room and given a mild electric shock. At the same time, the researchers shone a light on the brain cells that were active when the mice were in the first room. This made the mice associate the fear of the shock with the memory of the first room.

When the mice were put back in the first room, they showed fear, even though they had never been shocked there. Tonagawa described this as ‘implanting’ a false memory. He believes a similar process can happen in humans, who often have thoughts and ideas happening in their brains independently of the real world. This can lead to linking unrelated things together, creating a false memory.

Music services like Spotify and Deezer have made over $1 billion worldwide, as more people pay to listen to music online.

In 2013, money earned from streaming and subscriptions increased by more than 50% to $1.1 billion. This helped overall music sales in Europe to grow for the first time in 12 years, according to data released in March 2014.

There are now about 450 music rental services globally. Although many people still listen to music for free, more music fans are choosing to pay for a better experience and more choices. In three years, the number of paying subscribers increased from 8 million to 28 million, according to a report from the International Federation of the Phonographic Industry (IFPI) in 2014.

These services are easy to use on smartphones and tablets, and they allow people to discover new music without buying songs or CDs. People like them because they are cheap, easy to use, and legal – a good alternative to downloading music illegally. Frances Moore, head of the IFPI, said that streaming and subscriptions are now a main part of the music business. 

In Britain and America, streaming is starting to earn more money for the music industry than downloading music from stores like iTunes. Globally, subscriptions now make up one third of all digital music sales, with downloads making up the rest. However, subscriptions are growing faster than downloads.

One of Britain’s most expensive houses, called The Towers, is falling apart. Bird droppings cover the outside, skeletons of pigeons lie inside, and water leaks through the roof. This £30 million palace is on “Billionaires’ Row” in north London, and its condition has been kept secret until now.

Ten large houses on The Bishops Avenue, in north London, have been mostly empty for around 25 years. It is believed they were bought for members of the Saudi Arabian royal family. The houses are falling into disrepair – columns are breaking, and swimming pools are full of rubbish. Owls now live in some of them.

The Bishops Avenue is the second most expensive street in Britain, but many of its houses are empty. Sixteen mansions are unoccupied, some with locked gates and metal coverings on the windows. Guard dogs patrol the grounds. Another empty house is worth £18 million but has broken windows and paint to stop people climbing over the walls. A house that sold for £20 million also has metal bars on the windows.

Despite this, house prices continue to rise. One house, Dryades, sold for £12 million in 2007 and is now worth about £30 million. Heath Lodge, where a man was murdered in 1984, is now worth £13 million, after being bought for £400,000 in the 1970s.

To Tua Pittman, a traditional navigator from the Cook Islands, a canoe is more than just a boat. He says a canoe represents an island, the people on board are like a community, and the navigator is the leader. He believes leadership skills are important both on a canoe and in a country.

Recently, Tua and a crew of around 100 people sailed four canoes from the Cook Islands to Sydney, Australia, for the World Parks Congress. They started their journey on September 25th, stopping in Samoa, Fiji, and Vanuatu along the way. They wanted to use only traditional navigation methods, using the stars, moon, sun, and birds to guide them. However, they sometimes had to use modern equipment to arrive on time.

Their voyage, called the Mua Voyage, was a partnership between several organizations and Pacific Island countries. The goal was to share an important message with the World Parks Congress about the health of the ocean.

The message explained that overfishing and pollution are damaging the ocean. They have noticed fewer fish and the destruction of coral reefs and mangrove forests. They warned that the ocean, while large, is not unlimited and is struggling to support life due to growing populations and unsustainable practices.

At the Congress, discussions focused on how much of the ocean should be protected. In 2013, only about three percent of the world’s oceans were protected areas, and less than one percent had strict protection. A previous goal set in 2003 was to protect 20-30% of the ocean, but many felt this wasn’t enough.

Dame Sally Davies, England’s Chief Medical Officer, has compared antibiotic resistance to the danger of terrorism. This may seem extreme, but the threat from antibiotic resistance is actually greater. Each year, more people die globally because of bacteria that are resistant to antibiotics than die from terrorist attacks.

It’s difficult to measure the full impact of antibiotic resistance, but the World Health Organization estimates that over 150,000 people die each year from tuberculosis that is resistant to drugs. Antibiotic resistance is now a serious problem, like a war.

Over the last 100 years, people in the UK live much longer. In the early 1900s, men lived to around 47 years old and women to 50, with many children dying young from infections. Today, a child born in Britain has a good chance of living to 100. This is thanks to public health, vaccines, and antibiotics, which help us prevent and treat diseases caused by tiny organisms.

I work in intensive care, where antibiotics are used a lot. These drugs kill ordinary bacteria, but they leave behind stronger bacteria that can survive. These bacteria learn to resist the drugs.

When I became a doctor in the late 1990s, I learned about MRSA, a bacteria resistant to many common antibiotics. We had a few strong drugs like vancomycin and teicoplanin to fight it, but bacteria quickly became resistant to these too. We kept needing new, stronger drugs, and it felt like an ongoing battle.

People from Rwanda and neighbouring Burundi travel to the town of Butare to visit a small shop called Inzozi Nziza, which means “Sweet Dreams”. They go to try ice cream, something many have never tasted before.

This shop is the first ice cream parlour in the country. Customers can choose flavours like sweet cream, passion fruit, strawberry, and pineapple. They can also add toppings such as fresh fruit, honey, chocolate chips, and granola. The shop also sells black tea and coffee.

The manager, Louise Ingabire, says the shop is popular and is “changing lives”. She explains that ice cream is new to many Rwandans, and they are learning to enjoy it. 

Inzozi Nziza helps people achieve their dreams. A 27-year-old employee says she didn’t have a job before, but now she earns money and can support her family.

The shop uses local ingredients as much as possible. Milk comes from a nearby town, but vanilla and cocoa are imported.

A new study by the World Health Organization (WHO) shows that 30% of women have been attacked by a partner. Also, 38% of women who are murdered are killed by their partners.

The study found the highest levels of violence in Africa, where almost half of all women (45.6%) will suffer violence. In poorer countries in Europe, 27.2% of women experience violence. However, even in wealthier countries, a third of women (32.7%) will experience violence in their lifetime.

The sale of a Banksy mural was stopped just before it was going to be sold at an auction in Florida. The artwork, called ‘Slave Labour’, shows a child making flags and was a comment on a celebration last year. It was expected to sell for around $700,000.

The owner of the auction house, Frederic Thut, had not said where the artwork came from. He announced that ‘Slave Labour’ and another Banksy piece had been removed from the sale. He didn’t explain why.

Local leaders in Haringey, London, had been campaigning to stop the sale of the mural, which was taken from a shop wall. They were pleased the auction had been halted. Alan Strickland, a local councillor, said they were halfway to getting the artwork returned. Claire Kober, the leader of Haringey Council, had asked officials in England and Miami to intervene.

Some people have accused the auction house of selling stolen property, but Thut said the seller was the rightful owner and the sale was legal. He also said he had received many angry messages from the UK.

This was because a newspaper, The Sun, had previously published untrue stories about the disaster. These stories were given to the newspaper by the police, who were trying to avoid blame for what happened and wrongly accuse the people who died.

Facebook is losing users in some of its biggest markets, like the US and UK, according to recent data. In the last month, Facebook lost 6 million users in the US and 1.4 million in the UK. Over the last six months, the US saw a loss of nearly 9 million users, and the UK lost 2 million. This is also happening in countries like Canada, Spain, Germany, France and Japan.

Experts believe most people who want to join Facebook in the US and UK already have accounts, and some users are looking for new social networks. Other platforms, like Instagram, are becoming more popular, especially with younger people. One new network, Path, is gaining 1 million users each week.

However, Facebook is still growing quickly in South America and India. In Brazil, users increased by 6% last month, reaching 70 million. In India, users rose by 4% to 64 million.

Other reports also show a decline in Facebook use. One study found that the number of minutes people in the US spend on Facebook fell from 121 billion in December to 115 billion in February.

Facebook has said that people are using smartphones and tablets more, which means they are spending less time on Facebook using computers. While smartphone use is increasing, it’s not clear if this will make up for the decrease in computer use.

Facebook will soon tell investors about its performance. Experts expect the company to announce a 36% increase in revenue, reaching around $1.44 billion. Investors will be interested in how quickly Facebook’s mobile user base is growing and if advertising revenue is still increasing.

Vienna is considered the best city in the world for quality of life, while Baghdad is ranked the worst. A recent international study showed that cities like London, Paris, and New York are not even in the top 35.

Cities where German is spoken do very well in the study. Vienna is joined by Zurich, Munich, Dusseldorf, and Frankfurt in the top seven. Paris has fallen to 37th place, and London is 39th, mainly because of concerns about terrorist attacks.

The study looked at things like income, health, education, housing, and the environment. Companies use this information to decide where to locate their businesses and how much to pay their employees.

Helena Hartlauer, who was born in Vienna, wasn’t surprised by the results. Vienna has a long history of investing in good, affordable housing. She lives in a large apartment close to the city centre and pays only €800 a month in rent. A similar apartment in London would cost over £2,000, and even more in New York.

Cities in the US generally did not score well, often because of safety and crime issues. San Francisco was the highest-ranked US city at 28th, followed by Boston at 34th. Cities in Canada, like Vancouver, performed much better than those in the US.

Hartlauer says Vienna is a very safe city with excellent public transport. A single trip on the underground costs only €1, and it runs 24 hours on weekends.

Ouarzazate, a city in Morocco, is famous for being a location for many films. It’s near the Sahara Desert and is the centre of Morocco’s film industry, nicknamed “Ouallywood”. Now, the city is building a large solar power plant.

This plant will have four connected parts and will use sunlight, water, and wind to create almost half of Morocco’s electricity by 2020. Morocco hopes to sell any extra electricity to Europe. The project is part of a plan to make Morocco a world leader in solar energy, using the power of its deserts.

When finished, it will be the biggest concentrated solar power plant in the world. The first part, called Noor 1, started working in November 2015. It uses mirrors to collect sunlight. This technology is more expensive than solar panels on roofs, but it can still produce electricity even when the sun isn’t shining.

Scientists have known about the potential of desert solar power for many years. After the Chernobyl accident in 1986, a scientist calculated that deserts receive enough energy in a few hours to power the world for a year. The problem was finding a way to collect and transport this energy.

Now, 500,000 curved mirrors are shining in the desert near Ouarzazate. These mirrors follow the sun throughout the day. The completed plant will cover an area as large as the capital city, Rabat, and will produce enough electricity for a million homes. Noor 1 alone can power 160,000 homes.

Swedish prisons are known for being different from those in many other countries. In 2013, the head of Sweden’s prison service, Nils Oberg, announced that four prisons would close because there were fewer prisoners.

Although crime rates didn’t fall, the number of prisoners in Sweden decreased by 6% between 2011 and 2012, to just over 4,500. They expected this decrease to continue. Oberg thought this might be because of the focus on helping prisoners change their lives and not re-offend.

Kenneth Gustafsson, who manages Kumla Prison, Sweden’s most secure jail, explained that prisons used to focus more on treating prisoners well. However, after some prisoners escaped in 2004, security became more important. 

Even with increased security, Sweden still tries to be humane. Prison sentences are usually no longer than ten years. People with life sentences can ask to have their sentence reduced after ten years, usually to between 18 and 25 years. Sweden was the first country in Europe to use electronic tags to monitor criminals. They also try to avoid short prison sentences, preferring community service which is more effective at preventing re-offending.

Sweden’s re-offending rate is between 30 and 40% after three years, much lower than in the UK. The traditional idea of working eight hours a day in Japan is changing. Many employees finish their most important tasks but don't go home, fearing it might seem disloyal.

For years, Japanese companies have expected workers to be completely dedicated, pushing them to work very hard. Now, the government is considering a new law to make companies allow employees to take at least five days of paid holiday each year.

Currently, Japanese workers are entitled to around 18.5 days of paid holiday, plus 15 national holidays, which is similar to the global average. However, most workers only use about nine days. Unlike in countries like Britain, where a two-week summer holiday is common, many Japanese workers feel guilty about taking even a short break.

This change is being discussed in parliament after some companies even encouraged employees to nap at work to improve performance. The government hopes the new law will encourage Japanese workers to take more time off, similar to British workers who take an average of 20 days and French workers who take 25 days.

Japan’s strong work culture helped it become a successful economy, and its workers are known for their dedication. However, this has often come at the cost of their personal lives.

Rob Yarrell, the manager of the aquarium, said that octopuses are known for escaping. He doesn’t think Inky was unhappy at the aquarium, but that he was curious and wanted to explore outside. 

Staff believe Inky slid across the floor of the aquarium – about three or four metres – and found the drainpipe. This pipe led directly to the sea in Hawke’s Bay. It’s also possible he squeezed into a pipe at the top of his tank, which went to the drain.

Yarrell was surprised to find the tank empty the next morning, but he hasn’t looked for Inky. The staff were sad, but they knew Inky was a special octopus who often surprised them.

Noma has been named the best restaurant in the world several times. The chef, René Redzepi, says ants taste like lemon, and some insect mixtures taste like fish sauce. A major reason for this is the increased use of shale gas in the US. Research from the International Energy Agency (IEA) shows that coal use is growing worldwide, even in countries trying to reduce carbon emissions. However, in the US, shale gas has replaced coal, lowering prices and making coal more attractive to use in other places, like Europe.

Coal is plentiful and can be easily and cheaply obtained in many parts of the world, unlike oil and gas. In the last ten years, it has provided almost half of the increase in global energy demand. Many people don’t get enough sleep, but there might be a simple solution: starting the day later. Dr Paul Kelley, a researcher at Oxford University, suggested that schools should change their start times to match students’ natural sleep patterns. He believes this would help students perform better in school, get better exam results, and improve their health. Not getting enough sleep can lead to health problems like diabetes, depression, obesity, and a weaker immune system.

By sixteen, this is later, around 8:00 am. And at eighteen, teenagers naturally wake up around 9:00 am. So, a school start time that works for a ten-year-old might not work for older students. Dr Kelley suggests that older teenagers might learn better if school started at 11:00 am or even later. He explains that making a sixteen or eighteen-year-old wake up at 7:00 am is like making a teacher in their fifties wake up at 4:30 am.

He emphasizes that it’s not just about telling teenagers to go to bed earlier. Our bodies have a natural rhythm controlled by light. Special cells in our eyes send signals to a part of the brain called the suprachiasmatic nuclei, which controls this rhythm over a 24-hour period. Felix Baumgartner jumped from the edge of space above the deserts of New Mexico. It was a 24-mile drop to Earth. Mission control said, “Our guardian angel will take care of you,” and he jumped.

Ten minutes later, he landed back on Earth, having reached speeds of up to 725mph. He broke three world records, including becoming the first person to break the sound barrier while skydiving (Mach 1.24). His mother, Ava Baumgartner, cried with joy as the control room cheered, “We love you Felix!” Baumgartner had broken the records for the highest balloon flight and the highest skydive, and he raised his arms in victory.

Later, he told reporters that when he was at the top, he felt humble and wasn’t thinking about records. He just wanted to get back alive, but added that going so high made him realise how small he was.

Barack Obama returned to Washington on Wednesday after giving a speech in Chicago celebrating his re-election. He asked the country to come together and support him.

In his speech, Obama said people voted for action, but it may be difficult to achieve. He will likely face opposition from Republicans who control the House of Representatives for at least two more years. There are important issues to solve, like government spending and national debt – known as the “fiscal cliff”.

Unlike after his first election in 2008, Obama may not have an easy start to his second term. Both the Republican leader in the House, John Boehner, and the Democratic leader in the Senate, Harry Reid, said they want to work together. However, disagreements are still possible.

Although Obama won the election against Mitt Romney, winning many important states, the country remains divided. Obama began working on his second term immediately. He wants to be remembered as a great president and address issues like the economy, immigration, education, and climate change. He also wants to improve foreign relations with countries like Iran, Israel, and Palestine.

Obama received more than the 270 electoral votes needed to win, and also more individual votes overall. Boehner said both parties need to find common ground to help the economy and reduce debt. Obama reportedly called Boehner to start discussions. Reid also expressed a willingness to work with Republicans.

Obama hopes to reach a large agreement with Republicans, something they failed to do in 2011. However, disagreements over spending – Republicans want to protect military spending, while Democrats want cuts – could cause problems. Obama wants to raise taxes on high earners, but Boehner opposes this.

This happened after police raided the Baur Au Lac hotel in Zurich. Among those accused were Ricardo Teixeira and Marco Polo Del Nero, both former leaders of the Brazilian football federation.

Finally, I breathed in deeply, and gasped for air. I managed to hold my breath for one minute and 12 seconds, which I was pleased with.

Holding your breath is important in some sports, like freediving. In 2006, I filmed a TV programme about lungs for the BBC. I met Sam Amps, captain of the UK freedive team. She taught me exercises to help me hold my breath longer underwater. By the end, I could hold my breath for 90 seconds – long enough to swim across a pool. Sam could swim three widths of the pool and hold her breath for five minutes!

I asked her how she did it. She said she breathes slowly for several minutes before diving, then takes a deep breath. She also said that training helps her hold her breath for longer than most people.

Some people believe our ability to hold our breath shows that our ancestors spent time in the water. They suggest humans can slow their heart rate and use less energy to hold their breath longer. They also link things like our lack of hair and how we walk on two legs to a time when humans lived in the water. However, the idea that humans evolved from aquatic apes isn’t supported by scientific evidence. It’s an interesting idea, but not a fact.

Galina Zaglumyonova was woken by a large explosion in her flat in Chelyabinsk, Russia. The explosion broke her balcony windows and knocked over her plants. She looked outside and saw a long vapour trail in the sky and heard car alarms ringing. She thought a plane had crashed.

The explosion was caused by a ten-tonne meteorite falling to Earth. Almost 1,200 people were injured, and over 40 were taken to hospital, mostly because of broken glass caused by the shockwave. Luckily, no one died.

The event caused panic in Chelyabinsk, a city of over one million people. Many people tried to call for help, so the mobile phone network became very busy. Videos showed the pieces of the meteorite glowing as they fell.

Another piece of the meteorite fell into a lake, breaking through the ice. Officials said there was no dangerous radiation.

Glastonbury Festival is working to reduce the number of plastic water bottles used at the event, as part of a plan to become the most environmentally friendly music festival in the world.

Each year, around one million plastic bottles are used at the 900-acre festival in Somerset, leaving a lot of plastic waste. To help solve this problem, festival organizers will give 2,000 staff and musicians reusable stainless-steel bottles. They will also sell more to visitors, encouraging them not to buy plastic bottles. The 140,000 people attending are being asked to bring their own reusable bottles and fill them at over 400 water taps around the festival site.

Lucy Smith, who works on environmental issues for Glastonbury, said that the UK has good quality water, but many people prefer to buy bottled water. She explained that this is the first step towards replacing all plastic cups and cutlery with reusable items by 2015, to reduce plastic waste.

Environmental groups say there are currently 150 million tonnes of plastic polluting the Earth and its oceans, harming animals and plants. Plastic bottles can take hundreds of years to break down, and making and transporting them uses a lot of oil and creates pollution. In the UK, about 13 billion plastic water bottles are sold each year, but only one in five is recycled.

Instead of buying bottled water, Glastonbury visitors are encouraged to drink tap water, which comes from underground reservoirs. The charity WaterAid will also have stands selling reusable bottles and cups, and offering free water refills. In 2015, these stands will also be used as DJ booths in the evenings.

In 2016, the world celebrated the 400th anniversary of William Shakespeare’s death. While many people know him through his plays performed globally, his hometown of Stratford-upon-Avon wanted to highlight his connection to the area.

Some believe Shakespeare left Stratford to find success in London, only returning to die. However, Paul Edmondson, from the Shakespeare Birthplace Trust, argues Stratford was very important to him. Shakespeare bought property and kept his books there, and likely did much of his thinking and writing in Stratford.

Even someone who knew Shakespeare, John Aubrey, admitted the playwright wasn’t particularly special, but noted his acting skills and the popularity of his plays. 

The anniversary was marked with performances around the world. In Singapore, they performed *Macbeth*, and in Brussels, *Romeo and Juliet*. Shakespeare’s Globe theatre even took *Hamlet* on a world tour. In London, a temporary cinema showed all of Shakespeare’s plays. Many theatres across Britain put on special performances, from traditional versions to more unusual shows. There were also lectures, concerts, and exhibitions.

There isn’t much information about Shakespeare’s life, so the survival of his plays is thanks to his friends and fellow actors who collected everything they could find – early drafts and notes – and published them in 1623 in a book called the First Folio. Actor Mark Rylance loves this book, and many original copies will be on display.

An exhibition called “By Me, William Shakespeare” will show important documents, including his will, papers about the building of the Globe theatre, and records of payments he received for performing for the King and Queen.

In August, Facebook reported that one billion people – about one in seven people on Earth – used the website in a single day. Mark Zuckerberg, the founder of Facebook, said the network has greatly changed many things in the last ten years, including how people relate to each other, their privacy, businesses, and the news.

Zuckerberg believes a more connected world is a better world, leading to stronger relationships, a better economy, and a stronger society. Here are some of the ways Facebook has changed things:

**1. The meaning of “friend” has changed.**

The word “friend” is now used as a verb, meaning to add someone on Facebook. It’s easy to stop being friends with someone online ("unfriend"), unlike in real life where ending a friendship can be difficult. Facebook has also changed how we think about the words “share” and “like”. We can easily see what old classmates and friends are doing, so reunions aren’t as important. We also know about their lives before seeing them in person. 

However, Facebook doesn’t show the importance of different friendships. A school friend you haven’t seen in years is treated the same as your closest family member. Some experts believe this could make it harder to maintain real relationships, as it’s so easy to end online friendships.

**2. People are less concerned about privacy.**

Facebook is free to use, but users are essentially the product. The company makes money by collecting information about its users, and many people willingly share it. Studies show that most young people are happy to share photos, their location, email addresses, and even phone numbers. This information allows companies to target advertising effectively. Poor countries will continue to be most affected by climate change over the next 100 years. They will experience rising sea levels, stronger storms, hotter temperatures, less predictable rainfall, and longer, more intense heatwaves.

Scientists previously thought temperatures could rise by 6°C or more by the end of the century. Now, they believe a rise of around 4°C is more likely. Even this smaller rise could seriously damage crops and make life difficult in many cities.

A new report from the Intergovernmental Panel on Climate Change (IPCC) says that rainfall patterns will change significantly in tropical and subtropical areas. East Africa will likely have more short rains, while West Africa will have heavier monsoon seasons. Countries like Burma, Bangladesh, and India can expect stronger cyclones, and other parts of Asia will see heavier summer rains. Indonesia might have less rain during certain months, but areas around the South China Sea could experience more extreme rainfall when storms arrive.

The report also states that countries in Europe and North America will probably receive more rainfall, but many dry regions will likely get less. In wet, tropical areas, rainfall will become more intense and frequent. Monsoon seasons are also expected to become longer.

Scientists in developing countries welcome the report, saying it confirms what they have already observed. Saleemul Huq, from the International Centre for Climate Change and Development in Dhaka, said that developing countries are already experiencing the effects of climate change and don’t need a report to tell them the weather is changing.

Sea levels are now predicted to rise by 40-62 cm by 2100, depending on future greenhouse gas emissions. This threatens millions of people in cities like Lagos and Calcutta.

Some men experience a feeling of sadness around middle age, and sometimes react by making big changes, like buying a sports car. This is often called a midlife crisis. Now, scientists think this might not be unique to humans.

An international team of scientists studied chimpanzees and orangutans and found that these apes also seem to experience a drop in happiness during middle age. They published their research in a scientific journal.

The scientists asked people who care for the apes – zookeepers and researchers – to answer questions about the animals’ moods, social lives, and how well they achieved goals. They scored the apes’ well-being on a scale of one to seven. They studied over 500 apes from zoos and sanctuaries in several countries.

The results showed that the apes’ well-being decreased in middle age, then improved again as they got older. For chimpanzees, this low point was around 28 years old, and for orangutans, it was around 35 years old. Apes in captivity can live to be 50 or older.

Scientists believe this drop in well-being might be caused by changes in the brain that also happen in humans, or because apes who are less happy may not live as long. However, apes don’t make the same big lifestyle changes that humans sometimes do during a midlife crisis.

Some other scientists are not sure about the findings. They question whether apes can even experience a midlife crisis, as they don’t plan for the future in the same way humans do. Another scientist believes there is not enough evidence to prove that a midlife crisis exists even in humans.

When you think of the word “Amazon”, do you imagine the rainforest, the river, or the online store? This question is important in a debate about how the internet is controlled.

Brazil and Peru are objecting to Amazon, the company, trying to register “.amazon” as a new internet address. Currently, addresses end in “.com” or “.org”, but new addresses are being considered.

The South American countries say that if Amazon owns “.amazon”, it will be harder to use this address to protect the rainforest, help local people, or for other important public purposes. They believe a company shouldn’t control a name that refers to a large geographical area within their countries.

Amazon has applied for many new internet addresses, like “.shop” and “.book”. However, “.amazon” is causing the most disagreement. Brazil and Peru want the application to be rejected. They argue that private companies shouldn’t profit from geographical names.

Other countries are also protesting new internet addresses. Argentina is unhappy that Patagonia, a clothing company, is trying to register “.patagonia” because Patagonia is a famous region in Argentina with important resources and a local community. China is also objecting to “.shangrila”, saying it refers to a region in their country.

The Internet Corporation for Assigned Names and Numbers (ICANN), an organization that helps manage the internet, has received many applications for new addresses. Each application costs almost $200,000. 

ICANN’s advisory committee asked for a pause on the disputed addresses in April. They will discuss the issue again in July. The first new internet addresses could be used by the end of 2013.

The sounds of nature are at risk of being lost to future generations because people are blocking them out, according to a US researcher.

Kurt Fristrup, a scientist at the US National Park Service, says increasing background noise is making it difficult for people to hear natural sounds like birdsong, flowing water, and rustling leaves – even in cities. He explained that people often listen to music with headphones instead of paying attention to the sounds around them, which makes the problem worse.

Fristrup believes people are “learning to ignore” important sounds. He warned that we could lose our ability to hear well and to connect with the environment.

For ten years, the National Park Service has measured sound levels in over 600 places, including parks like Yosemite, Yellowstone, and Denali. They found that human activities – like planes, motorbikes, and buses – create noise in every location.

Fristrup’s team combined this data with information from cities and predicts that noise pollution is increasing faster than the population, doubling every 30 years. He understands why people use headphones to block out noise, but says this reduces our ability to experience all the sounds around us, like looking through fog.

Fristrup fears that people will get used to increasing noise levels and forget how quiet the world could be. He believes many children may grow up without experiencing peaceful, natural sounds.

Other scientists have found that listening to natural sounds can be good for our health. Derrick Taff, from Pennsylvania State University, conducted experiments showing that people recovered from stressful situations faster when they listened to recordings of nature sounds – like waterfalls and birdsong – compared to recordings of traffic or conversations.

India’s richest people are expected to become much wealthier in the next few years. A new report says their wealth will increase four times between now and 2018, and many new millionaires will be created through businesses and inheritances. This prediction comes as business confidence grows in India, the world’s largest democracy.

Although India has recently faced economic difficulties like slow growth and rising prices, the Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) won a big election victory in May 2014, promising to improve the economy. The report from Kotak Mahindra Bank shows that there are almost 16% more Indians with over $3.75 million now than in 2013. Murali Balaraman, who wrote the report, says that cities are growing, the middle class is increasing, and there are more opportunities, with a better political situation.

Currently, India’s richest people have around $1 trillion in assets, which is about a fifth of the country’s total wealth. By 2018, this is expected to rise to $4 trillion, creating three times as many millionaires.

Abhay Gupta, from Luxury Connect, believes this market will continue to grow, as many people admire the wealthy and try to copy their lifestyle.

Thatcher was the first woman to lead a major western country. She was prime minister for 11 years, the longest time since 1827. She was 87 years old and had been ill with dementia for some time. She stopped speaking in public after having some strokes in 2002.

Nick Clegg, the deputy prime minister, said Thatcher was a very important figure in British politics and left a lasting impact on the country.

Sir John Major, a former prime minister, said she was courageous and determined, and kind and generous in private.

For over three years, all students at the school have walked or run a mile every day, at different times during the school day, and they seem to enjoy it. Importantly, none of the children at the school are overweight, even though many children in the UK have weight problems.

The “daily mile” has greatly improved the children’s fitness, behaviour, and ability to focus in class. Because of this, many other schools in Britain are now doing the same thing, encouraging students to get up and move for 15 minutes each day by walking or running around the school or a nearby park.

Elaine Wyllie, the headteacher at St Ninian’s, receives around two emails a day from schools wanting to know how they do it. She is pleased that other schools might use this idea to help children across the country get more exercise.

Statistics show that one in ten children are overweight when they start school. A study in 2015 also showed that English schoolchildren were less fit than ever before. This is why schools have been quick to try the “daily mile”. It has already started in schools in London, Wales, and other parts of Scotland, with more schools planning to introduce it. In Stirling alone, 30 schools are already doing or will soon start the daily mile.

How close are we to seeing drones deliver our online shopping? Amazon believes it could happen soon, but others aren’t so sure. They say it’s not just about building the drones, but also about making sure it’s safe for everyone.

Paul Misener, from Amazon, told a government hearing that his company is ready to start deliveries as soon as the rules are set. He joked about sending a basket of fruit by drone to show how it works.

The Federal Aviation Authority (FAA) will have rules for using drones for business by June 2016. However, these rules will only cover smaller drones, weighing up to 25kg. The FAA also says that all drones need to use different radio signals so they can’t be interfered with or controlled by others.

Professor Sajiv Singh, who runs a drone delivery company, explains that flying a drone isn’t simple. It’s like giving it directions step-by-step. Even short flights can be difficult, especially delivering to homes in cities or suburbs. Drones might face unexpected problems like new buildings or blocked GPS signals.

These problems can be solved, but it’s not easy. One challenge is keeping contact with the drone and knowing what to do if the connection is lost. If a standard drone loses contact, it will simply fall to the ground. Engineers are working on fixing this, but it’s not yet standard practice.

Jay McConville, from Lockheed Martin, says drones shouldn’t be complicated to control. Operators want to see important information about the drone and a video feed on their devices, not lots of technical details.

Technically, most of the technology needed for drone delivery already exists.

PizzaExpress keeps 8p from every £1 of tips paid by card as an administration fee. The Unite union estimates this earns the company around £1 million each year. PizzaExpress has 430 restaurants in the UK and is popular with families.

Chantal Chegrinec from Unite says the fee is unfair and PizzaExpress should give staff all the tips customers give them. She added that other companies also take money from tips, and they will protest at those restaurants too.

The first protest will be at the PizzaExpress near the British Museum in London. Unite has also written a letter to the company’s CEO, Richard Hodgson. This campaign started after a survey of PizzaExpress staff, who said the fee was a major concern. The survey was done after a company called Hony Capital bought PizzaExpress in 2014.

One PizzaExpress worker said the fee costs her £3 each night. She has worked at PizzaExpress for 15 years and earns the national minimum wage of £6.50 per hour, so she relies on tips to earn more money.

PizzaExpress is not the only restaurant that takes money from card tips. Ask and Zizzi also take 8%, while Café Rouge, Bella Italia, Belgo, Strada and Giraffe take 10%.

The National Security Agency (NSA) has been secretly accessing information from major US internet companies like Google, Facebook and Apple. This is part of a program called PRISM.

A secret document shows that PRISM lets the NSA collect things like search history, emails, file transfers and live chats. The document is a 41-page presentation used to train intelligence officers. It claims the NSA can get information directly from the companies’ servers. 

However, the companies say they didn’t know about this program. Google said they only share user data with the government when required by law. Apple said they had “never heard” of PRISM. Several company leaders said they would not be involved in such a program.

The NSA gained this access because of changes to US surveillance laws, first made under President Bush and continued under President Obama in 2012. These laws allow the NSA to monitor communications of people outside the US, and also potentially communications within the US without a warrant.

This information comes after another leak revealed the NSA was collecting phone records from millions of Americans. Unlike just collecting phone numbers, PRISM allows the NSA to see the content of communications.

The program started in 2007 with Microsoft, and other companies joined over time, including Yahoo, Google, Facebook, YouTube, Skype and Apple. Together, these companies control most online communication.

US law requires companies to give information to the government when asked, but PRISM allows the NSA direct access to their servers. Some senators were worried about this level of surveillance when the law was renewed in 2012. They thought the NSA needed the companies’ permission to access data, but PRISM makes that permission unnecessary.

Do you want your child to be successful in sports? A new study suggests that children born in November or October may have an advantage. Researchers found that students born in these months are generally fitter than their classmates.

The study, led by Dr. Gavin Sandercock, looked at over 8,500 boys and girls aged 10 to 16 from schools in Essex, UK. They tested the students’ fitness levels in three areas: stamina, strength, and lower-body power. The results showed that children born in the autumn months (October, November, and December) were stronger, faster, and had more energy than children born in other months, especially those born in April or June.

For example, a boy born in November could run 10% faster, jump 12% higher, and be 15% more powerful than a boy of the same age born in April. These differences could be important when choosing athletes for sports teams.

Children born in November were the fittest overall, while those born in October were the strongest. Children born in April and June were generally the least fit. This could mean they are less likely to be chosen for school sports teams.

Researchers believe this happens because babies born in the autumn get more vitamin D during the last months of pregnancy. Vitamin D, which comes from sunlight, is important for health and development. 

The study also found that children born earlier in the school year often do better in school, and now it seems they may also be better at sports. However, experts say that good physical education classes and early experiences with sports are also very important for developing skills like agility and balance.

Singer Kate Bush recently asked her fans not to use phones at her concerts. It has been 35 years since she last performed, and she noticed how much things have changed – now many concerts are filled with people looking at screens.

Bush wants to perform in a small theatre so she can connect with the audience. She wrote on her website that she wants people to enjoy the show with their eyes, not through their phones. She hopes everyone can share the experience together. She also wants to keep the show a surprise for fans who haven’t seen it yet.

Other artists have also complained about phones at concerts. Roger Daltrey from The Who thinks it’s strange when people watch a show through their phone screens instead of enjoying the performance. Beyoncé once told a fan to stop filming and enjoy the moment.

Fans at sports events also feel strongly about this. Some fans of the PSV Eindhoven football team protested against wi-fi in their stadium, wanting people to focus on the game. Manchester United has asked fans not to film with tablets.

Musicians like Jarvis Cocker and Johnny Marr believe phones stop people from truly experiencing the music. Cocker says it drives him “insane”, while Marr thinks fans miss out on the atmosphere when they try to record everything. The band Yeah Yeah Yeahs even put up a sign asking fans to put their phones away.

Even classical musicians are affected. Pianist Krystian Zimerman once left the stage because someone was filming him, saying YouTube is ruining music.

Scientists are warning that the world may need to eat mostly vegetarian diets by 2050 to avoid serious food shortages. Currently, people get about 20% of their protein from meat, but this may need to decrease to only 5% to feed the expected population of nine billion people.

According to research from the Stockholm International Water Institute (SIWI), there won’t be enough water to grow food for nine billion people if current farming and eating habits continue. The report says we can avoid shortages if meat makes up only 5% of our diet, and if countries can trade food to help each other.

This warning comes as organizations like Oxfam and the UN worry about another global food crisis. Prices for foods like corn and wheat have increased by nearly 50% since June because of droughts in the US and Russia, and poor rains in Asia. Over 18 million people in the Sahel region of Africa are already facing food shortages.

Oxfam believes rising food prices will badly affect developing countries that buy a lot of food from other countries, including parts of Latin America, North Africa, and the Middle East. Food shortages in 2008 caused problems in 28 countries.

Scientists say becoming vegetarian is one way to save water, as producing meat requires much more water than growing vegetables. One-third of farmland is used to grow food for animals. Other solutions include reducing food waste and improving trade between countries.

The town of Kiruna in northern Sweden is having to move because of an iron-ore mine. The mine is so large that it’s causing the ground under the town to collapse. Residents face a difficult choice: stop mining and lose jobs, or move the entire town to safety.

Kiruna was built in 1900 because of the mine, and the town has become wealthy from the iron ore found there. However, the very thing that created Kiruna is now threatening to destroy it. The mine produces 90% of all the iron in Europe and is still growing, as demand for iron increases worldwide.

In 2004, the mining company warned that the town was in danger. The mine shafts are angled towards the town, and this is causing cracks to appear in buildings. After ten years, these cracks are getting closer to homes and businesses. This has made life difficult for people in Kiruna, who can’t make long-term plans.

The city has a plan to move everything about 3 kilometers to the east by 2033. They are building a new town centre with a new town hall and will move 20 important buildings, piece by piece. Kiruna’s historic church will be a central feature of a new park. However, some places that are important to residents, like the bench where they first kissed or the hospital where their children were born, will be lost.

The mining company is providing £320 million to build new facilities like schools and a community centre. However, people are worried about where they will live and how housing will be allocated. Currently, people in Kiruna pay low rent and earn good wages, but this

Collecting phone records through government programs is a threat to people’s privacy, according to US researchers. They showed how basic phone logs can reveal personal details about individuals.

The researchers at Stanford University used anonymous data about calls and texts – but not the content of the messages – to find out people’s names, where they live, and who their partners are. They were also able to discover sensitive information. For example, they found one person owned a rifle, another had an irregular heartbeat, and one person was pregnant while another had multiple sclerosis.

This information is called “metadata” and includes numbers called, the time of the call, and its length. When combined with information from websites like Google, Yelp, and Facebook, metadata can reveal a lot about a person’s life. Security services have long known this, and one former NSA official said metadata can tell you “everything about somebody’s life.”

The researchers wanted to show the public how much information metadata contains, as many people were unaware. They asked 823 people to share their phone metadata through an app, collecting data on over 250,000 calls and 1.2 million texts. They also used information from the participants’ Facebook accounts to confirm their findings.

Initially, analysts could look at phone records up to three connections away from a person, going back five years. Now, this has been limited to two connections and 18 months.
