Angela Erdmann never met her grandfather, as he died in 1946, before she was born. However, on April 8th, 2014, she received an amazing message – a bottle containing a note he had thrown into the Baltic Sea 101 years earlier. The museum now exhibiting the bottle in Germany believes it is the oldest message in a bottle ever found.

Erdmann, 62, explained how she found out about the bottle. A man came to her door and said he had mail from her grandfather. He explained that a bottle with a message inside had been discovered, and the name on the message was her grandfather’s. The man was a researcher who had found Erdmann in Berlin after the bottle was given to the International Maritime Museum in Hamburg.

The brown beer bottle had been in the sea for 101 years when fisherman Konrad Fischer caught it off the coast of Kiel. Holger von Neuhoff, a museum curator, said this was the oldest bottled message he had ever seen. While older documents have been found, this is the oldest complete message with its bottle. He also noted the bottle was in very good condition.

Researchers believe Erdmann’s grandfather, Richard Platz, threw the bottle into the sea during a nature walk in 1913, when he was 20 years old. 

Most of the postcard inside was difficult to read, but the address in Berlin was clear. The author asked whoever found the bottle to send it to his home. He also included two old stamps so the finder wouldn’t have to pay for postage. However, he didn’t expect it would take 101 years to be delivered

The person standing next to you in the shop queue might seem like a normal customer. But look closely – instead of a shopping list, they might be taking notes about how clean the store is or how the staff behave. They could also be timing how long the queue takes, and perhaps even filming with a hidden camera. This person is likely a ‘mystery shopper’.

In the UK, around 50,000 mystery shopping visits happen every month. As more people shop online, companies are using mystery shoppers more and more. Simon Boydell from Marketforce explains that people who visit shops want a good experience they can’t get online. Companies want to know how well their stores are providing this experience.

Mystery shoppers are sent to different stores and don’t usually visit the same one again for three months. Jill Spencer from ABa says shoppers often visit five to ten shops a day, spending up to eight hours. They then spend a few more hours writing detailed reports. They can earn up to £155 a day, plus money for travel costs, hotel stays, and wear and tear on their car. Those who film their visits can earn around £300 a day.

Shoppers are usually given money to spend in the shops and may be allowed to keep what they buy. Laura, from Devon, has visited around 7,000 shops since 2001. She’s usually given £5 to £20 to test the service at the checkout. She has to buy something specific, but can often choose what she wants and keep it.

Over one million people in Britain may be working on zero-hours contracts, according to new research. This means companies are using these contracts more than previously believed.

The research, from the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development (CIPD), has led to calls for the government to investigate how these contracts are used. Recently, several organizations, including shops and Buckingham Palace, have been criticised for hiring staff without guaranteeing them a fixed amount of work or pay. People on zero-hours contracts don’t always receive holiday or sick pay, and may need permission to work elsewhere. The CIPD found that 38% of workers on these contracts consider themselves full-time, working over 30 hours a week. One-third of charities and one in four public sector organisations use them.

These new numbers mean that official estimates of zero-hours contracts may be inaccurate. The Office for National Statistics has increased its estimate by 25%, to around 250,000 workers.

Peter Cheese, head of the CIPD, said there needs to be a clearer understanding of what zero-hours contracts mean and how they are used, considering both the benefits and problems for businesses and workers.

Sports Direct, a retailer, recently faced criticism because around 20,000 of its 23,000 workers are on zero-hours contracts. Other companies, like Cineworld cinema and Buckingham Palace (for its 350 summer workers), also use these contracts. Pub group J D Wetherspoon employs 24,000 staff – 80% of its workforce – on these terms.

There are now more tigers in Nepal than there have been since the 1970s, according to a new count. This gives hope to people working to protect tigers, as their numbers have been falling across South Asia for the last 100 years.

The survey showed there are now 198 Bengal tigers in Nepal, which is a 63.6% increase in just five years. Maheshwar Dhakal, an ecologist, said this is “very encouraging.”

The count was done using pictures from over 500 cameras in protected areas and wildlife corridors. More than 250 experts worked on the survey, which cost around £250,000.

A similar survey was also done in India, and the results will be published later in 2013. India currently has about 1,300 tigers in large protected areas.

Nepal promised to double the tiger population from 121 (the number in 2009) by 2022. However, increasing wealth in Asia has made tiger skins and body parts more valuable. These are used in traditional Chinese medicine, and illegal gangs pay local people in Nepal to kill tigers. The skins and bones are then smuggled to India, where they are sold.

A problem is that some government officials are involved in this illegal trade. Experts believe the increase in tiger numbers in Nepal is due to better protection of national parks, stronger efforts to stop poaching, and better management of tiger habitats. Nepal’s forests cover 29% of the country. However, they say more needs to be done to protect the areas where tigers live and the animals they eat.

Louise Haggerty, 56, went to a Sainsbury’s supermarket at 1am for Black Friday sales, but she wasn’t sure she even wanted what she bought. She picked up a Dyson vacuum cleaner. She said the store was very crowded and chaotic, and people were pushing each other.

She originally wanted to buy a flat-screen TV, but it was impossible to get close enough in the queue. She saw someone pushed by a group of young people and they didn’t get anything. She only saw two security guards. She ended up buying the vacuum cleaner, even though she didn’t know the price and wasn’t sure she would keep it. She said some people had three or four TVs, which she didn’t think was fair.

Andy Blackett, 30, was more successful. He bought two coffee makers, two tablets, two TVs and a stereo. His friend, Henry Fischer, 19, wasn’t so lucky – someone took the TV he was trying to buy because he was smaller.

Blackett and his friends first went to a Tesco supermarket, but it was too chaotic, so they went to Sainsbury’s instead.

At the Tesco store, police had to intervene because people were fighting. Customers were pulling down barriers to get to the sale items. Tesco delayed selling TVs for almost an hour until the police could control the crowd. One police officer said the manager should have provided more security and suggested stopping the sale. This Tesco store had problems with riots during a sale in 2005.

Barack Obama encouraged young people to be hopeful and talk to people with different opinions if they want to improve the world. 

Speaking to 500 young leaders in London during his last visit to Britain as US president, Obama said people should believe they can make a difference. He quoted John F. Kennedy, saying problems are created by people and can be solved by people.

He told students that they have the tools to create change, but it needs effort, determination and belief. He also recognised the difficulties young people face, mentioning events like 9/11 and the constant flow of negative news online.

Obama discussed his policies on healthcare and education. He stressed the importance of talking to people who disagree with you, as it helps with finding solutions. He also encouraged them to continue working for change, even if progress is slow. He said the fight for justice takes time, quoting Martin Luther King Jr.

Obama said he was proud of his healthcare changes and the way the US dealt with the 2008 financial crisis. He also highlighted agreements with Iran and the response to the Ebola virus as successes during his time as president.

He was asked about the TTIP trade agreement and said that countries should not isolate themselves, but should protect workers’ rights.

Before the event, people expressed their excitement about hearing Obama speak. One person hoped to ask him about making it easier for people to vote.

Obama answered a question from a young man who talked about being treated differently at airports because of his religion. Obama said it’s important to accept people from all backgrounds and that American Muslims are strong allies.

Millennials are known for using technology a lot. More than eight out of ten sleep with their phones near their bed. Almost two thirds text while driving, and many use social media. A 2010 report showed 75% of millennials have a social media account, compared to 50% of Generation X, 30% of baby boomers, and only 6% of people aged 65 and older. However, not all millennials use social media.

Celan Beausoleil, 31, is a social worker from California who often stops using Facebook. She last left the site in 2015 because she felt overwhelmed by seeing so much personal information from others, on top of her demanding job. She explained that listening to people’s problems all day made it too much to also see details of everyone’s lives online. However, she did appreciate how social media connected people from all over the world. She realized she was spending a lot of time looking at friends of friends, and wondered what she could achieve if she used that time differently.

Mathias, who works for the government in Baltimore, deleted his Facebook and Twitter accounts in 2012. He quickly forgot about them. He understands the benefits of social media, like easily getting to know people at parties, or organizing events. But he now enjoys having more free time. He reads books and news articles instead of scrolling through social media, and he prefers to call friends instead of connecting with them online.

Large predators like brown bears, wolves, and lynx are increasing in number across Europe, according to a new study. This is surprising because many people thought these animals would disappear due to growing human populations.

The study found these animals live in almost one-third of Europe, including countries like Sweden, Finland, and Spain. Importantly, most of them live outside protected nature reserves, which means conservation efforts are working. There are around 17,000 brown bears, 12,000 wolves, 9,000 lynx, and 1,250 wolverines in Europe. 

Some countries, like Belgium, Denmark, the Netherlands, Luxembourg, and Britain, do not have breeding populations of these large animals. However, researchers believe Britain could support these predators. They have even found wolves living in areas with high population densities – sometimes more people per square kilometre than in cities like Cambridge or Newcastle.

Researchers found that wolves, lynx, and bears can live in areas with a significant number of people. For example, wolves live in areas with 37 people per square kilometre, lynx with 21, and bears with 19. This shows that people and predators can share the same land.

This approach, called “land-sharing,” is different from creating separate wilderness areas. It means managing conflicts between people and predators, and finding solutions to problems they cause. The success in Europe is due to several factors, including political stability, increasing numbers of animals that predators eat, and financial support for farmers to protect their livestock – like using electric fences.

Doñana National Park in southern Spain is a beautiful and important area for birds. It covers 200,000 hectares of wetlands and is home to around 200,000 birds, including many that migrate from Africa. It’s a UN World Heritage Site and provides a home for rare animals like the Spanish imperial eagle and the Iberian lynx.

However, Doñana is in danger. In 1998, a dam broke at a mine called Los Frailes, releasing almost two billion gallons of toxic waste into the park. This caused a major environmental disaster, killing thousands of fish and birds, and costing €90 million to clean up. 

Spain then invested another €360 million, including money from the EU, to repair the damage. Some farmland that had been drained to grow crops was returned to wetland. While this work has been positive, the park still faces threats. There are plans to build an oil pipeline and expand tourist resorts, which would use a lot of water. Pollution from nearby farms is also a problem.

Recently, the local government decided to reopen the Los Frailes mine, which caused the 1998 disaster. Conservation groups, like the RSPB, are very worried. They say the park is vital for birds, but reopening the mine could cause another disaster.

The local government says reopening the mine is necessary because the area has high unemployment (over 30% in some places). The mine would create over 1,000 jobs. In the UK, restaurants are not legally required to give tips to their staff. In 2016, the government started a review to look at how tips are handled, asking workers, employers, and customers for their opinions. The government wants to make rules to ensure that workers receive the tips left by customers.

The review found that some restaurants charge waiters a fee – up to 15% – when tips are paid by credit or debit card. Some waiters even have to use their own money to cover these fees if there aren’t enough tips to go around. The government is considering making it illegal for employers to take any money from workers’ tips.

The government also wants restaurants to be clearer about their tipping policies, so customers know that tipping is optional.

Rodri, from London, says that tips make up around 50% of a waiter’s income. He earns about £60 in tips per eight-hour shift, and believes the US has a fairer system. He explained that some restaurants take 4% of food sales as a fee, meaning a waiter could have to pay from their own money if a customer doesn’t tip.

Elle, from Edinburgh, works multiple part-time jobs. She says it’s often unclear whether she’s receiving a fair share of tips, especially when paying by card. She thinks France has a better system, where waiters have secure jobs and earn a good salary without relying on tips.

Tea, baked beans on toast, and fish and chips are traditional British foods. However, a recent study shows that eating habits in the UK have changed a lot over the years. The study used information from the National Food Survey, which began in 1940 to check people’s health and food access.

The amount of tea people drink has fallen by more than half since the 1970s. In 1974, people drank about 23 cups a week, but now it’s only eight. Although tea is still the most popular hot drink, people now spend more money on coffee.

The study, which looked at 150,000 households between 1974 and 2014, also found some healthier choices. People are drinking more low-calorie drinks, switching to skimmed milk, and eating more fresh fruit. But, they are also eating more chips, pizza, crisps, and ready-made meals.

Bread choices have changed from white to brown and wholemeal, but people are eating less bread overall – about 15 slices a week now, compared to 25 slices four decades ago. Baked bean consumption has decreased, but people are eating more Italian food like pasta and pizza. Pizza consumption has risen from none in 1974 to 75g per week now, and pasta consumption has almost tripled.

People are also using fewer potatoes, with consumption down by 67% since 1974. They are eating more other vegetables like cucumbers and mushrooms. Takeaway food has almost doubled, with chips and meat being the most popular choices.

Agios Efstratios is a very remote island in Greece. It’s so isolated that mobile phones don’t work for data, and there are no cash machines or places that accept credit cards. Life was good before Greece had financial problems. People used the post office for banking, and the island’s few rooms to rent were always full in the summer. Visitors came because of the beautiful, empty beaches, clear water, and fresh seafood.

However, the lack of banks has caused serious problems. Because the island relies on cash, the closure of banks across Greece has been devastating. Residents now have to travel nine hours to get cash from a larger island, and fewer tourists are visiting. “Tourist numbers are down 80% this year,” said the Mayor, Maria Kakali. Even people who were born on the island and have homes here aren’t coming.

The Mayor has asked the government and a bank to provide a cash machine, but she worries it will be too late for the summer season. Tourism is much more important to the island than fishing or farming. There are very few bookings for August, when usually the island is very busy. A new harbour project with 50 workers might help in the winter, but there’s another problem: the government plans to end a tax reduction for islands.

This tax reduction was created to help island communities when many people were leaving to find work. It kept the cost of living lower because everything had to be brought to the island by boat, and it made tourism more affordable. Popular tourist islands like Mykonos are worried losing the tax break will make them less competitive with Turkey, but for Agios Efstratios, it’s a much bigger threat.

Scientists have connected the brains of two rats, allowing them to share information and work together. This is a big step towards creating what the scientists call an “organic computer”.

The team from the US used special devices called brain-to-brain interfaces. These devices allowed the rats to complete simple tasks together to get a reward, like a drink of water. In one test, the rats were in different locations – one in the US and one in Brazil – and connected through the internet.

The research is led by Miguel Nicolelis, who has previously developed technology to help people control computers and robotic arms with their thoughts. He believes this new work could allow many brains to connect and share information. He says they have created a direct connection between brains, and this is like building an “organic computer”.

The scientists connected the rats’ brains using tiny electrodes, which are small electrical connections. They trained the rats to press a lever when a light turned on. When a rat pressed the lever, information from its brain was sent to the other rat. The second rat then correctly pressed the lever about 70% of the time, using the information it received.

The rats could also communicate with each other. If one rat failed to complete the task, the other rat would change its behaviour to help. They also worked together to figure out the difference between small and large openings using their whiskers.

Even when the rats were on different continents, they could still share information over the internet. The scientists said this shows it’s possible to create a network of animal brains in different places.

Thousands of people protested on beaches in Australia against a shark cull in Western Australia. They asked the state’s leader to stop the cull, and organizations like RSPCA Australia and Richard Branson, who owns Virgin Atlantic, also criticized it.

The cull began after several shark attacks on the Western Australian coast. In November 2013, a 35-year-old surfer was killed, making him the sixth person to die in a shark attack in two years. However, on average, only one person in Australia dies from a shark attack each year.

Kate Faehrmann, from the Sea Shepherd Conservation Society, spoke at a protest in Perth, the capital of Western Australia. She said the cull wouldn’t work because the drumlines used to catch sharks also harm other animals like dolphins and turtles. Protests happened in cities including Perth, Sydney, Adelaide, Victoria and Queensland, showing many Australians want to protect sharks.

Anthony Joyce, a surfer who was once bitten by a shark, believes killing sharks won’t solve the problem. The government hasn’t said how many sharks have been killed, but some people report that smaller sharks caught on drumlines were released. These drumlines are floating drums fixed to the seabed with bait on hooks.

Experts say there’s no proof the cull will reduce attacks, as no other cull has used only drumlines. Researchers at the University of Western Australia think the increase in attacks might be because Western Australia’s population is growing quickly, not because there are more sharks.

The International Monetary Fund (IMF) asked the United States to improve its financial situation after the country avoided a possible failure to pay its debts. This happened after a 16-day shutdown of many government offices, during which hundreds of thousands of workers were temporarily out of work.

US President Barack Obama said the country needs to stop dealing with problems at the last minute. Christine Lagarde, head of the IMF, also asked for more financial stability. She said the US needs to make it easier to raise the debt limit in the future. She also encouraged the US to approve a budget for 2014 and find ways to reduce spending without harming the economy, and to create a long-term financial plan.

A deal was made in the Senate and then passed by the House of Representatives just before the deadline to raise the debt limit. This deal didn’t give much to the conservatives who had caused the financial problems.

The World Bank also expressed relief that a major economic problem had been avoided. Its president, Jim Yong Kim, urged all countries to focus on policies that help the economy grow and create jobs.

Stock markets in Japan, China, Hong Kong, and South Korea initially rose when Republicans finally agreed to end their attempt to change Obama’s healthcare plan. However, markets in Asia and Europe didn’t react much overall, as people expected another financial fight in Washington in 2014.

The shutdown is estimated to have cost the US $24 billion, according to the ratings agency Standard & Poor’s. China’s news agency criticized the US for putting other countries’ money at risk, as China is the largest holder of US debt.

Sudan is the last male northern white rhino in the world. He lives in a protected area in Kenya with two female northern white rhinos. Scientists are trying to get them to have a baby, but it is difficult because Sudan is old and previous attempts have failed. There are only two other northern white rhinos left, and they both live in zoos.

Even though Sudan is so rare and protected by armed guards, poachers still try to kill him for his horn. Rhino horn is illegally sold in Asia and is wrongly believed to be a medicine. Sudan’s horn has already been cut off to try and stop the poachers, but they still pose a threat.

Sudan seems unaware of how important he is. He spends his days walking around the reserve with his guards. He is a very strong animal, but also vulnerable.

Rhinos haven’t changed much over time. A drawing of a rhino made in 1515 looks very similar to Sudan. People have been fascinated by rhinos for centuries. Even ancient people admired them, as shown by paintings of woolly rhinos in caves from 30,000 years ago. Sadly, these ancient people also contributed to the extinction of those rhinos.

Today, rhinos are still being killed by poachers. While there are more southern and black rhinos, the northern white rhino is the most endangered. Poaching has increased dramatically in recent years – in 2014, over 1,200 rhinos were killed in South Africa alone. 

The northern white rhino is almost extinct, and other rhino species are also in danger. India has managed to protect its rhino population, but poaching remains a problem.

Now, everyone is interested in the 24th Bond film, called *Spectre*. People are asking if *Spectre* will be as successful as *Skyfall*. 

Charles Gant, a film expert, believes *Spectre* is heading in the right direction. He says *Skyfall* was clever because it appealed to both long-time fans and new audiences. The title *Spectre* will also attract fans who enjoy the classic Bond films, while still keeping the newer audience interested.

The company that makes the Bond films, Eon Productions, was founded in 1961. They are trying to make *Spectre* as successful as *Skyfall* by using the same creative team, including the writer and director, Sam Mendes. Mendes is known for making films that focus on characters, and he has helped make the Bond series even more popular. He also works with talented actors like Ralph Fiennes.

*Skyfall* earned almost twice as much money as the previous Bond film, *Quantum of Solace*. Eon Productions wants to repeat this success. 

Before Mendes and actor Daniel Craig joined the series, some people thought the Bond films were becoming predictable. The films had moved away from the original stories by Ian Fleming, and the series needed something new.

An international agreement to make clothing factories in Bangladesh safer is facing possible legal problems. Factory owners want to be paid for the costs of closing factories and repairing them. They say they cannot afford to pay workers while factories are closed, and also need money for the expensive repairs to make the buildings safe.

These repairs started after the Rana Plaza factory in Dhaka collapsed in 2013, killing 1,138 people. Now, hundreds of factories are checked every month for safety issues like fire risks and building problems. This is done through the Accord on Fire and Building Safety in Bangladesh, which is supported by over 170 international brands – like Primark and Marks & Spencer – and trade unions.

One factory owner in Dhaka, from Softex Cotton, has threatened to take legal action against the Accord because his factory was closed due to structural problems. He is asking for $100 million in compensation. Another owner said that if a factory closes, even for a few months, it will lose business and close forever. He believes the Accord did not clearly explain who would pay for factory closures when the agreement was made after the Rana Plaza disaster.

Jenny Holdcroft, from the IndustriALL trade union, said the agreement guarantees factories will still receive orders while closed, as brands have promised to continue working with suppliers for two years. She also said that many factories only need partial closures, allowing production to continue on some floors. The Accord also requires brands to pay workers during closures. She explained that details about who would make the payments were left open to encourage factory owners who could afford to contribute to do so.

Oxfam reports that the huge wealth of the world’s 100 richest people is increasing inequality and making it harder to fight poverty. The charity says that this wealth has increased greatly, often by reducing secure jobs and fair wages for poorer people. This makes it difficult for those living on low incomes or relying on aid to improve their lives.

Oxfam calculates that if the richest 100 billionaires gave away the money they earned in 2012, it would be enough to end extreme poverty four times over. In 2012, these billionaires earned a total of $240 billion.

Although some wealthy people, like Bill Gates and Warren Buffett, donate a lot to charity, this is not common among billionaires in countries like Russia, China, and the Middle East.

In a report published before the World Economic Forum, Oxfam asks world leaders to reduce extreme income differences and lower inequality to levels seen in 1990. The report shows that the richest 1% have increased their income by 60% in the last 20 years, and the financial crisis made this worse.

Barbara Stocking, head of Oxfam, says extreme wealth is harmful to the economy, politics, society, and the environment. She explains that when workers earn less, investment and economic growth suffer. She believes that creating wealth for a few does not automatically help everyone, and often the opposite is true.

David Cameron said the result of the Scottish independence referendum was clear, with Scotland voting against becoming independent from the rest of the UK. 55.3% voted against independence, while 44.7% voted for it. The vote means Scotland will remain part of the UK after 307 years.

Cameron promised changes across the UK, including allowing English MPs to vote on issues that only affect England. He said the decision of the Scottish people should be respected and there would not be another referendum.

Alex Salmond, Scotland’s first minister, accepted that Scotland had voted to stay in the UK “at this stage”. He said he would work with the UK government to improve things for Scotland.

The ‘yes’ campaign, which wanted independence, did well in some areas like Glasgow and Dundee. However, the ‘no’ campaign, which wanted to stay in the UK, won overall in 28 areas, including Edinburgh.

Cameron said any changes to how the UK is governed will not happen until after the next general election. He wants to make sure that people in England, Wales and Northern Ireland are also considered.

Other political leaders also reacted. Ed Miliband, the Labour leader, said the vote showed people in Scotland wanted change. Nick Clegg, the deputy prime minister, said the result should lead to wider changes in how the UK is governed.

Some Conservative MPs may disagree with Cameron’s promise to give Scotland more powers. Nigel Farage, from the UK Independence Party, said England should also have more power.

Brazilian singer Anitta has become very popular, bringing the music of the favelas (shanty towns) to a wider audience. However, she is now at the centre of a discussion about skin colour and how it affects success.

Some people believe Anitta has changed her appearance to become more acceptable to the white, middle-class market. They point to photos showing her skin looking darker when she was unknown, and paler after she signed a record deal. It’s unclear if this change is due to skin-lightening products, cosmetic surgery, or editing in photos. This has started a debate about whether being lighter-skinned is necessary to succeed in Brazil.

Jarid Arraes, a student and blogger, wrote that Anitta’s change shows a lack of acceptance of black people in the media. He says that in Brazil, white people are often seen as successful and good, while black people are not.

Anitta, whose real name is Larissa de Macedo Machado, used to sing in a church choir. She became known as a dancer and singer in Rio de Janeiro’s baile funk scene. She is now famous with a hit song, “Show das Poderosas,” which has over 52 million views on YouTube.

Her supporters say she connects the favelas with wealthier areas. She has changed her style, making it less shocking than traditional baile funk. However, some wonder if she has changed too much to appeal to a wider audience. Arraes believes that pop stars are often pressured to change their appearance, like straightening their hair or getting plastic surgery, which can damage their self-esteem.

This is a sensitive issue in Brazil, a country with a large population of people with African ancestry

In 2005, Pope Benedict XVI said he arrived as “a simple worker for God”. On a cold February Monday, he announced he was resigning in a similar way – like an older worker who could no longer manage the physical demands of the job. He spoke in Latin, as was his custom.

He timed his announcement carefully. He told cardinals in the Vatican that on February 28, 2013, the position of Pope would be vacant, and they would need to begin choosing a new Pope.

Monsignor Oscar Sanchéz Barba, from Mexico, was present. He said everyone was surprised and speechless when the Pope announced his decision. The cardinals looked at each other in disbelief, as they believed the Pope was God’s representative on Earth.

Angelo Sodano, a senior cardinal, gave a short speech, saying they were shocked by the news. The Pope then blessed everyone and left. Sanchéz Barba described the scene as simple and quiet, filled with sadness.

John Thavis, a journalist who had reported on the Vatican for 30 years, believed the Pope might resign and returned to Rome expecting it. He remembered the Pope saying in a 2010 interview that he would resign if he was no longer able to do the job. Thavis had guessed February 22nd as the resignation date, but was wrong.

People at the Vatican said the Pope’s decision was brave. He was facing the reality that modern medicine can keep people alive even when they are too weak to lead a large organization. Thavis agreed, saying it was courageous for the Pope to resign while still healthy, simply because he was tired.

Kamal, a refugee from Sudan, comes to classes for three or four hours each day. He says learning French is difficult, but important. “It helps to keep my brain active and maybe achieve my dreams,” he explains.

Many refugees are living in a camp near Calais, waiting for France to accept their request for asylum. They want to learn French to help them live in their new country. 

Kamal is annoyed that news reports only show people trying to cross the English Channel to the UK. He wants people to know that many refugees want to stay in France.

France has accepted more than 250,000 refugees, which is more than twice the number accepted by the UK, even though both countries have a similar number of people living in them. There are another 56,000 people waiting for a decision on their asylum request in France, and 36,000 in the UK.

While they wait, France doesn’t give refugees money or allow them to work. So, many choose to live in the basic conditions of the camp for a few more months, rather than risk being refused asylum by working illegally.

In the Canadian Arctic, the summer sun shines for more than 20 hours a day. This is welcome for some, but creates difficulties for Muslims during Ramadan, the month when they fast from sunrise to sunset.

Abdul Karim, who lives in Iqaluit, Nunavut, has been carefully timing his fast since moving from Ottawa in 2011. This year, he eats before 1:30am and breaks his fast around 11pm. He says he will only stop fasting if it harms his health.

Ramadan is usually a time for community, prayer, and thinking. But in Arctic communities like Iqaluit, the long daylight hours have changed how people fast.

Most Muslims in Iqaluit follow the fasting times of Ottawa, which is 1,300 miles south. Muslim scholars say people in the far north can use the times from Mecca or a closer Muslim city. This means fasting for about 18 hours a day, says Atif Jilani, who moved from Toronto in 2015. He finds it long, but manageable.

The 100 Muslims in Iqaluit often share a meal together in their new mosque, eating traditional foods like dates and curry while the sun is still shining.

Similar scenes happen in other northern mosques. In Yellowknife, Muslims have several options for fasting. They can follow times from nearby cities, Mecca, or Medina. Many now use the times from Edmonton, Alberta. Nazim Awan, who leads the Islamic Centre, follows Mecca times to make it easier for his 12-year-old son to fast for about 15 hours.

The Senate Intelligence Committee has approved a bill about the National Security Agency’s collection of US phone records. The bill would allow the NSA to continue collecting phone data, but with more transparency. The NSA would be able to collect records for 90-day periods and keep them.

Some politicians want phone companies to hold this data instead. The committee voted 11 to 4 in favour of the bill, meaning it can now be discussed by the full Senate.

The bill says analysts can look at the data if they have a reasonable suspicion someone is connected to terrorism. It also allows the NSA to continue watching foreigners in the US for up to 72 hours.

This bill disagrees with another one, proposed by Senator Patrick Leahy, which would stop the collection of phone records. Senator Mark Udall also opposed it, saying it doesn’t change things enough. He believes the NSA’s surveillance doesn’t respect people’s rights and needs bigger changes. Another Senator, Ron Wyden, said the bill doesn’t offer meaningful reform.

Dianne Feinstein, who supports the bill, said the NSA’s program is legal and helps national security. She also said more transparency is needed to gain public trust. 

The bill would require the NSA to publish a yearly report about how often they search the phone data and how often it leads to investigations. It would also limit who at the NSA can access the data and set up penalties – up to 10 years in prison – for illegally accessing it.

Feinstein strongly supports the NSA program, saying it’s vital for protecting the country.

Noise from ships may be causing more problems for whales and dolphins than scientists previously believed. New research shows that ship noise can interfere with these animals’ ability to communicate and find food.

For a long time, scientists have known that large whales are disturbed by the low-frequency rumble of ships. However, recent studies by US researchers have found that ships also create noise at higher frequencies, up to 20,000Hz – the range where killer whales (orcas) hear best. This noise can make it difficult for killer whales to use echolocation, which is how they find prey by bouncing sound off objects. Dolphins and porpoises, which also use high frequencies, may have the same problem.

This is especially concerning for the endangered population of just 84 killer whales that live off the west coast of the US and in Puget Sound. Even a small increase in noise can make echolocation harder, and these whales already struggle to find enough food, like chinook salmon.

Researchers used underwater microphones to measure the noise from around 1,600 ships passing through Haro Strait in Washington State over two years. The ships included cruise ships, container ships, and military vehicles. The average noise level near the ships was very loud – 173 underwater decibels, which is similar to 111 decibels in the air, like a loud rock concert. Although whales aren’t usually right next to ships, they still experience noise levels of 60 to 90 decibels, similar to a lawnmower or vacuum cleaner.

If you win the lottery, you might buy a new car, go on holiday, or buy a house – and that’s what usually happens, according to a study of lottery winners.

Since the lottery started in 1994, it has created 3,000 millionaires who have won a total of £8.5 billion, an average of £2.8 million each. These winners have also helped create another 3,780 millionaires among their family and friends.

Most winners (59%) stop working immediately. However, 19% continue with their jobs, and 31% do volunteer work. Good news for the UK economy is that winners spend 98% of their money within the country. This spending on things like houses, cars and holidays helps to keep around six people employed for a year for each winner.

Lottery winners have added almost £750 million to the UK’s economy (GDP) and have paid over £500 million in taxes. They spent £2.72 billion on main homes and £170 million paying off debts. 

They also spent £2.125 billion on investments to continue earning money. Winners gave £1.17 billion to family and friends, and spent £680 million on cars and holidays.

The study, which looked at 100 winners of over £1 million, found that the 3,000 winners have bought 7,958 houses or flats in the UK – an average of 2.7 each – spending £3.3 billion. Most winners (82%) moved to a new, bigger home

Scientists have learned a lot about people who lived before farming by studying DNA from a 7,000-year-old hunter-gatherer found in a cave in Spain. The man had a mix of features: blue eyes, dark or brown hair, and dark skin. This is surprising because scientists previously thought people in Europe had light skin at that time.

The man likely couldn’t easily digest milk or starchy foods. However, his DNA showed he already had genes that helped protect him from diseases. This suggests that changes in the human immune system weren’t only caused by farming, as some scientists believed. He had genes to fight off infections even before farming began.

The scientists were surprised by their findings. They expected to find different results. The remains of the man and another individual were very well preserved in the cool cave. They used DNA from the man’s wisdom tooth to create his complete genetic code – the first time this has been done for a European who lived before the farming era.

The DNA also showed a link between the hunter-gatherer and people living in northern Europe today, especially in Sweden and Finland. 

This discovery may change how artists picture people from this time period. Current images often show them with light skin, but this man had dark skin and blue eyes.

Experts believe this research highlights the importance of understanding diseases that existed before farming began and how they affected people’s health. It shows that life before farming wasn’t necessarily worse for people’s health, as was once thought.

It’s unusual to discover several new elements at the same time, but that’s what happened recently. Researchers in Japan, Russia, and the US have discovered four new elements. These are the first additions to the periodic table since 2011, when elements 114 and 116 were added.

These new elements are very short-lived and radioactive, meaning they break down quickly. They complete the seventh row of the periodic table and mean that science textbooks need to be updated.

The International Union of Pure and Applied Chemistry (IUPAC), which is the organization that officially names elements, confirmed the discoveries on December 30, 2015. The scientists had been studying these elements since 2004. Now, the scientists need to give the elements proper names, replacing the temporary names they currently have: ununtrium, ununpentium, ununseptium, and ununoctium. These temporary names are based on the element’s atomic number – the number of protons in its center.

IUPAC said that a team from Russia and the US discovered elements 115, 117, and 118. They gave credit for discovering element 113 to a team from the RIKEN Institute in Japan. This makes Japan the first Asian country to officially name an element. IUPAC allows elements to be named after myths, minerals, places, countries, or scientists.

He criticized some newspapers, saying he didn’t trust them and they often wrote untrue stories. He explained that his father, Prince Charles, often reminded him to act like a prince. 

As an army captain, Prince Harry said he attacked Taliban fighters to help protect soldiers and rescue injured people. He said he was just doing his job, and the helicopter often stopped attacks just by being present.

He described having different roles in his life: a soldier, a private person, and a member of the royal family. He said he changes between these roles when needed. He admitted sometimes behaving badly, which he blamed on spending more time as a soldier than a prince. He believes he deserves some privacy.

Prince Harry was very critical of the media, especially newspapers that usually support the royal family. He was annoyed by comparisons between his job and the work of pilots in World War II. He said he has always been suspicious of the media because of how they treated his family when he was young. He admits to reading stories about himself, but says they make him angry. His father and others always tell him not to read the newspapers.

He was in Afghanistan to control a very advanced Apache helicopter, which cost £45 million. These helicopters helped NATO soldiers fight the Taliban and rescued injured soldiers.

A new scientific study suggests that global temperatures will likely rise more than previously thought due to climate change. Unless we reduce greenhouse gas emissions, the Earth could warm by at least 4C by the year 2100. This is twice the level governments consider dangerous.

The research shows that as the planet warms, fewer clouds will form. This means less sunlight will be reflected back into space, causing temperatures to rise even further. Understanding how clouds affect global warming has been a major challenge for scientists.

Professor Steven Sherwood, who led the study, explained that it provides new information about what controls changes in clouds and suggests that earlier, lower estimates of future warming are probably incorrect. A 4C increase would be catastrophic, making life very difficult in many tropical areas and causing ice sheets in Greenland and Antarctica to melt, leading to significant sea level rise.

Other scientists agree this research is a major step forward. It reduces the uncertainty around how much warming is caused by carbon emissions. Hideo Shiogama and Tomoo Ogura said the explanation of fewer clouds forming is convincing and supports the idea that future warming will be greater than expected. However, they also noted that more research is needed to refine temperature predictions.

Scientists estimate climate sensitivity by predicting how much temperatures will rise if the amount of CO2 in the atmosphere doubles compared to pre-industrial levels. For twenty years, estimates have ranged from 1.5C to 5C. This new study narrows that range to between 3C and 5C, by focusing on the role of clouds.

Cities are having to rethink transportation because commutes are getting longer and roads are getting older. Simply making roads wider isn’t enough to solve problems like increasing population and pollution. Cities are now focusing on making transportation part of a larger plan to protect the environment.

Cities like Los Angeles, Seattle, and Chicago are adding more bus lanes, improving walkways, and expanding train lines. They are also working with companies to develop self-driving cars that can communicate with each other and with roads. Experts believe the best cities for living have different ways to travel – buses, trains, and bikes. A good transportation system is important for a city to be successful.

Every morning, before it gets hot, a group of friends meet in Delhi, India. They do stretching, breathing exercises, and meditation on the grass near the India Gate monument.

Arvind Singh, a 42-year-old salesman, says this is a healthy way to start the day. Similar groups are meeting in cities across India, using any available green space.

On June 21st – the International Day of Yoga – India’s prime minister, Narendra Modi, wants people all over the world to join in. He plans to hold a large yoga session near India Gate with around 45,000 people doing a 35-minute routine. 

Modi, aged 64, his government, and some famous people will participate. Organizers are inviting people from many countries to show that yoga is an international activity.

He also plans to make yoga compulsory for police officers and offer free lessons to three million government workers and their families. Air India will offer yoga training to new pilots. Some politicians even suggest yoga could help reduce sexual violence in the country.

Modi, who is a vegetarian and practices yoga himself, first suggested an international yoga day when he spoke to the United Nations in 2014. Leading music promoter Harvey Goldsmith believes the era of large British music festivals like Glastonbury may be ending. He has worked with many famous artists, including The Who, The Rolling Stones, and Queen.

He says the main problem is a lack of new, popular bands to replace older ones. He spoke at the Hay Festival in Wales, explaining that festivals reached their peak around two years ago. There are now too many festivals and not enough famous bands to perform at them. In 2014, there were around 900 music festivals in the UK, and he doesn’t think they can all continue.

Goldsmith predicts that festivals will change, offering more than just music – things like poetry, books, or magic shows. He believes people are tired of large, crowded fields with limited facilities.

He also notes that people listen to music differently now. They prefer individual songs instead of whole albums, which is how many rock bands became successful. 

Goldsmith is building a new 1,100-seat theatre in Wembley with Robin de Levita, who worked on The Who’s musical *Tommy*. The theatre will feature a special rotating stage and screen technology. Two islanders found a small boat on a remote Pacific island. Inside was a man who said he had been lost at sea for 16 months. He claimed he started his journey from Mexico, over 12,500km away.

The man was very weak and had long hair and a beard. He was wearing only shorts. He told the islanders he left Mexico for El Salvador in September 2012, but his boat’s engines didn’t have propellers. He said a friend died during the journey.

Ola Fjeldstad, a student researching the island, said the man’s name was José Ivan. He survived by catching turtles and birds with his hands. However, because he only spoke Spanish, it was difficult to get more details. There was a turtle inside the boat, but no fishing equipment. Fjeldstad described the boat as very old and damaged.

The islanders took José Ivan to the main island, which is very remote with limited communication. The mayor contacted the government in the capital city, Majuro. Officials are waiting for more information and plan to bring him to the capital. 

The only plane that can land on the island is being repaired, so officials might send a boat to rescue him. He is staying with a local family who are giving him food and water. He has low blood pressure but is able to walk with help. He is getting stronger.

A survival expert, Fraser Christian, said it’s possible to survive at sea for a long time, but it’s very difficult. He said it’s possible to catch turtles and small fish by hand. The biggest problems are a lack of water and protection from the sun.

SeaWorld’s profits have fallen by 84% as fewer people visit its theme parks. This is because of concerns about how the company treats its orca whales.

SeaWorld trains dolphins and killer whales to perform for visitors. However, the company has seen a decrease in visitors, sales, and profits. This is due to problems with its public image.

In 2013, a documentary called *Blackfish* showed claims that SeaWorld’s treatment of orcas caused them to become violent and led to the deaths of three people. After the documentary was released, fewer people visited the parks, the company lost money, and the CEO had to leave.

SeaWorld has started a marketing campaign to try and change people’s opinions. They say that orcas in captivity don’t live as long as those in the wild. They have spent $10 million on the campaign, which shows their veterinarians caring for the whales, and have also lowered ticket prices. 

However, SeaWorld’s CEO, Joel Manby, admits the company is still struggling to convince people that it cares for its whales well. He says it will take time and money to get visitor numbers and profits back to where they used to be. He also said they need to continue to correct false information.

Manby, who became CEO in 2015, plans to share his ideas for the future of SeaWorld on November 6th. The company is planning a new shark exhibit in Orlando and a dolphin swim attraction in San Antonio.

Dusty arrived in Doolin around 2008, and many people have swum with her since then, so she seems tame. She even appeared in an advertisement for Irish tourism, where a girl said she wanted to touch a dolphin.

That evening, the woman was touching Dusty’s belly, and it looked nice. About twenty people were watching from the pier. When I swam into the water, Dusty suddenly became very agitated. I later learned she protects the people she’s with and doesn’t like others getting close. She started hitting the water with her tail, and at first I thought she was playing. Then I realized she was angry. I tried to swim back to the pier, but Dusty quickly swam into me with her nose. It was very strong and painful, and she was very fast. I was thrown forward.

Everyone on the pier was shocked. Dusty was still swimming near me, hitting the water with her tail. I was scared because I thought she might hit me with her tail and pull me under the water. 

I reached the pier but couldn’t climb out because I was injured. I was very frightened and shouted for help. A man reached down and pulled me onto the steps. It’s becoming very common to see people using e-cigarettes, but it’s possible that their popularity is starting to decrease. Statistics suggest that vaping is becoming less common among smokers and people who have recently quit smoking – the main group of people who use e-cigarettes. This is important news for e-cigarette companies, who have spent a lot of money promoting their products.

In 2014, a health charity called Action on Smoking and Health (ASH) found that the number of adults in Britain using e-cigarettes almost tripled between 2012 and 2014, rising from 700,000 to 2.1 million. 

However, research from the Smoking Toolkit Study shows that vaping rates may be falling. Vaping among smokers and ex-smokers increased until the end of 2013, when around 22% were vaping. But this number stayed the same during 2014 and then dropped to 19% by the end of the year. Early data suggests this decline continued into 2015. Professor Robert West, who collects this data, says the drop is significant.

Most e-cigarette users (around 70%) are smokers. Very few people who have never smoked have tried vaping. Professor West says that fewer smokers are using e-cigarettes *while* continuing to smoke. He also notes that there hasn’t been an increase in the number of long-term ex-smokers or people who have never smoked taking up vaping.

Scarlett Johansson is taking a French novelist to court, asking for €50,000 because she believes his book contains false information about her life.

The book, called *The First Thing We Look At*, is by Grégoire Delacourt. It tells the story of a French model who looks very much like Johansson. In the book, the male character believes this model *is* Johansson. The novel describes how the model is seen as a sex symbol by men and is envied by women. She pretends to be Johansson and has many adventures before being discovered. Eventually, the character dies in a car accident.

Johansson is unhappy with the book. Her lawyer, Vincent Toledano, said the book illegally uses her name, reputation, and image. He also said it makes false and damaging claims about her private life. They are now asking the court to stop the book from being translated into other languages or made into a film. The court case started in Paris on Wednesday, but neither Johansson nor Delacourt was there.

Toledano explained that while Johansson supports freedom of speech, this book is only about making money and is not creative.

Delacourt says he mentioned Johansson because he thinks she is a beautiful woman. He insists his character is not meant to be Johansson.

The author recently said on French radio that he was sad about the lawsuit. He believes it is strange that a court can get involved with a fictional story.

Delacourt is a popular author in France. His previous book was translated into 47 languages and is being made into a film. He said he was surprised to learn Johansson was suing him, and he had hoped she would contact him for a coffee

Young people in Cuba are using a new, free internet service offered by a famous Cuban artist. This is the first service of its kind in the country. The cultural centre in Havana where it’s available has become a popular place to get online.

The artist, Kcho, is providing the free wi-fi. Surprisingly, the state-owned telecommunications company, Etecsa, has allowed him to do this. 

Although the internet speed is slow when many people use it at once, it is very welcome. Only about 5% of Cubans have full access to the internet, so a free and open service is considered a major improvement.

People are excited to use the internet to read news, connect with family abroad, and use social media like Facebook and Twitter. Adonis Ortiz, a 20-year-old, visits often to video chat with his father in the US, whom he hasn’t seen in nine years.

Cuba recently laid a high-speed cable from Venezuela to improve internet access, and some Chinese equipment is also being used. While around 25% of Cubans can access a limited, local internet network, this new service offers much more.

Kcho, whose real name is Alexis Leiva Machado, has connections with the Cuban government. He announced that the Ministry of Culture approved his plan. He wants to help Cubans learn how to use the internet, even though it is expensive – he pays around $900 a month for the service.

Kcho is a well-known artist who creates paintings, sculptures, and drawings. He became famous after winning an art prize in South Korea and is preparing for an art show in Havana. His art often features

After landing back on Earth from a record-breaking 340 days in space, astronaut Scott Kelly spoke to journalists. He said it felt like he had lived in space forever, and the biggest surprise was how long the mission seemed. He admitted that sometimes it was difficult to stay focused.

Kelly and Russian astronaut Mikhail Kornienko spent almost a year on the International Space Station (ISS) to study how space travel affects the human body. This research is important for NASA’s plans to send people to Mars one day. Kelly said the long mission was very challenging and he felt much more sore when he returned to Earth’s gravity than after shorter trips. 

Kelly and his twin brother, Mark, who is also a retired astronaut, have been having tests for a year to see how the body deals with the difficulties of space travel. Kelly felt pain and his skin was very sensitive, but his balance was mostly good. He even struggled to throw something onto a table at first, because he wasn’t used to gravity. 

He described the feeling of landing as amazing, despite the discomfort of returning to normal height after growing 1.5 inches in space. When the capsule opened in Kazakhstan, he smelled fresh air mixed with the sweet smell of the spacecraft. He realised how huge the ISS was – as big as a football field and weighing a million pounds. It uses energy from the sun and was built by an international team.

Kelly believes they will learn a lot from the research done on the ISS, comparing it to early computer science work at NASA. He also shared the beautiful views he photographed from space, including colourful cities, oceans, and the Himalayas. He was struck by how thin and fragile the Earth’

Junior Smart understands a lot about gangs. He is 36 years old and his life has two main parts. He explains that when he was a teenager, after his mother died, he joined a gang in south London. At first, the gang helped him feel less alone. But it soon became more serious, and they started to make money by doing illegal things.

Smart didn’t do well in his school exams, but he retook them at college and passed. He found a job and also worked as a DJ. However, he was still involved with the gang and making money illegally.

He was eventually arrested for serious crimes related to drugs and sent to prison for 12 years. He says this was a shock, as he thought he could avoid getting caught. He had been living two different lives – one with his friends and another with their enemies. It took him a long time to change his life.

Now, Junior Smart leads a team of 12 people and six volunteers. They help young people who are involved in gangs and crime to change their lives. Most of the team are ex-offenders themselves, and some are allowed out of prison during the day to help. They work with the police and other organizations to support people who feel scared and trapped in gangs.

Smart started this work when he saw that the prison system wasn’t helping people. He met a man with a drug problem who kept returning to prison. He realized that prisons didn’t deal with the reasons *why* people committed crimes, only the crimes themselves. For example, a man stealing to fund a drug habit wasn’t getting help with his addiction.

Wales is the first country in the UK to change the rules about organ donation. Now, people will be considered as having agreed to donate their organs after they die, unless they have said they don’t want to.

The Welsh Assembly voted for this new system. It means hospitals can use organs for transplant unless someone has registered to say they don’t want their organs to be used. The vote was 43 to 8, even though some religious groups and families were worried.

Mark Drakeford, the Welsh Health Minister, said this is important for the 226 people in Wales who are currently waiting for an organ transplant. He explained that many people don’t clearly tell their families about their wishes regarding organ donation, and this new law aims to help. Families will still be asked about the deceased’s wishes, and they can object if they believe the person wouldn’t have wanted to donate.

The government says there will be protections in place to make sure people’s wishes are respected. They also announced that families will have a stronger voice in the decision. Relatives can say if they believe the person who died would not have wanted to be an organ donor.

Wales has a shortage of organs for people who need transplants. About one person dies each week while waiting for an organ. Around a third of people in Wales are registered as organ donors, but more than two-thirds say they would be happy to donate. The new law will apply to anyone over 18 who has lived in Wales for at least a year. Organs can be used for people in Wales and other parts of the UK.

John Lewis, a department store, launched its 2015 Christmas advert featuring an old man living alone on the moon. The advert aims to raise money for the charity Age UK, which helps elderly people who may be lonely, especially during the holidays. John Lewis will also encourage its staff and customers to volunteer with Age UK.

The company spent £7 million on the campaign, including a TV advert, a smartphone game, and special products like glow-in-the-dark pyjamas. Eleven stores will be decorated to look like the moon.

The advert tells the story of a young girl named Lily who sees the old man on the moon through her telescope. She tries to reach him with letters and notes, and finally sends him a telescope attached to balloons. This allows them to connect. 

The advert’s message is “Show someone they’re loved this Christmas”, which supports Age UK’s message: “No one should have no one at Christmas”. Money from the sale of mugs, gift tags and cards will be donated to Age UK.

The song featured in the advert is “Half the World Away” by Aurora, a Norwegian artist. It cost £1 million to make the advert, and the moon scenes were filmed at the Warner Bros Studios, used for the Harry Potter films. The set was designed by someone who worked on the Star Wars film, *The Force Awakens*.

John Lewis used social media with the hashtag #OnTheMoon to create excitement before the advert was shown. It was a coincidence that there was a full moon on Christmas Day 2015.

Europe will be the first region to make car manufacturers test their vehicles’ emissions while driving on real roads, not just in laboratories. This is part of a plan to reduce air pollution.

Currently, cars are tested in conditions that are not realistic. The new rules will measure emissions while cars are driven in normal traffic. Researchers found that only one in sixteen cars meets the limit of 80mg of nitrogen oxide per kilometre. Countries like China and Korea are also considering similar tests and will be watching Europe closely.

Pollution from diesel engines causes at least 29,000 deaths each year in the UK, and this number may increase. The current laboratory tests are 25 years old and can be easily manipulated. For example, car companies have been known to use tricks like taping up windows or programming cars to reduce emissions only during the test.

Lucia Caudet, a spokesperson for the European Commission, said they are creating a new testing procedure to properly assess cars on the road. The plan needs final approval, but officials don’t expect major problems.

Greg Archer, from the organization Transport and Environment, explained that car companies have been cheating on tests, causing much more pollution on the roads. He believes the new tests are a good step towards cleaner air and that countries should support the plan, despite objections from car manufacturers.

Research shows that actual nitrogen oxide emissions from cars are seven times higher than the legal limit, and some cars produce 22 times more. Around one third of all nitrogen oxide pollution comes from vehicles, especially diesel cars.

Some cities have pigeons, but Lima, Peru has black vultures, also called gallinazos. These birds fly in groups and sit on old churches and buildings in the city centre. 

Many people in Lima don’t like the vultures because they remind them of the city’s problems with dirt, poverty and things being neglected. However, the authorities are now trying to show that these birds can be helpful. They are putting small cameras and GPS trackers on the vultures to help fight against illegal dumping of rubbish.

Samuel is one of ten healthy vultures being used in this project. He flies over the city and uses his strong sense of smell to find illegal rubbish dumps. The GPS tracker records the location of the rubbish on a map.

Alfredo Correa, Samuel’s trainer at Lima’s zoo, explains that vultures can eat dead animals safely because they have special bodies that protect them from viruses and bacteria. This project is a partnership between a US organisation (USAID) and the Peruvian government to help solve Lima’s rubbish problem.

The vultures have been given names like Capitan Huggin and Capitana Aella. A video shows them as heroes fighting against disease and pollution, while people ignore the problem. The project highlights a serious issue: Lima has only four official rubbish dumps for almost ten million people. About 20% of the city’s rubbish is dumped illegally. This waste pollutes the rivers that provide water for Lima, including the Rimac, Chillon and Lurin rivers.

Up to one billion people could still be living in extreme poverty by 2030 if countries don’t address inequalities. A recent report warns that many people may briefly escape poverty, but then fall back into it due to problems like drought, illness, or conflict.

The report found that in some areas of Kenya, South Africa, and Ethiopia, between 20% and 60% of people who left poverty later returned to it. Even countries like Indonesia and Vietnam have seen around 20% of people fall back into poverty. 

For example, Amin, a 61-year-old man from Bangladesh, has become poorer because of his and his wife’s illnesses, and family expenses. Lovemore, 74, from Zimbabwe, lost his job and now cares for his five grandchildren after his daughters died.

The report says governments need to help people stay out of poverty for good. Simply reaching a small income level isn’t enough. A UN panel believes ending extreme poverty by 2030 is possible, but “more of the same” efforts won’t be enough.

Progress in reducing poverty has been made – dropping from 1.9 billion in 1990 to 1.2 billion in 2010 – but future progress will be harder. China’s success may not be repeated elsewhere, and problems like climate change and poverty in Africa will slow things down.

The report emphasizes focusing on the ‘chronically poor’ – those who live in poverty for many years. It’s important to not only help people escape poverty, but also to prevent them from becoming poor in the first place, and to help those who have escaped

Currently, the most popular book on Amazon in the US is not a novel by a famous author. It’s a colouring book for adults by Scottish illustrator Johanna Basford. Her book, *Secret Garden*, has sold 1.4 million copies worldwide. Her new book, *Enchanted Forest*, has already sold over 225,000 copies.

Many celebrities, like actress Zooey Deschanel and K-pop star Kim Ki-Bum, have shared information about Basford’s books with their fans. Eleanor Blatherwick, from the publisher Laurence King, said they knew the books were beautiful but didn’t expect them to be so popular.

Other adult colouring books are also selling well. Richard Merritt’s *Art Therapy Colouring Book* is fourth on Amazon’s list in the UK, and Millie Marotta’s *Animal Kingdom* is seventh. Half of the top ten bestselling books on Amazon in the UK are now adult colouring books.

Publishers believe the trend started because people are looking for relaxing activities. Ana McLaughlin from Michael O’Mara, says their first adult colouring book in 2012 sold well, but sales increased a lot in 2014 with *Art Therapy*. She explains that the idea of reducing stress gave people a reason to enjoy colouring, even if they thought it was for children.

Basford says colouring is a creative and relaxing way to “unplug” from technology. She also thinks people enjoy the nostalgia of colouring, remembering doing it when their children were asleep. She originally created *Secret Garden* in 2013 because she wanted a colouring book for herself.

Margaret Allen leads exercise classes and is 93 years old. What makes her classes special is a tea break in the middle, where everyone can relax and have a drink with a piece of cake.

The class has about eight people, and Margaret herself stays energetic throughout, even though she has a painful leg and needs a knee replacement. During my visit, everyone enjoyed slices of fruitcake baked by Margaret’s 89-year-old sister, Joan, who is famous for her scones.

After the tea break, Margaret quickly gets the class moving again with lively exercises. She has been leading these classes for 45 years in a town near Middlesbrough. She started playing the piano for a class during the Second World War and took over teaching when the original instructor retired. Once, the class had over 18 members, each paying £1 to attend. However, the number of people coming is now decreasing, as one member recently died at the age of 68.

The youngest member of the group is 60-year-old Jean Cunion, who says the class helped her when her mother passed away. Another member, Ruth Steere, 76, is impressed that Margaret can tell if they are doing the exercises correctly, even with her back turned.

Margaret doesn’t have any formal training as a fitness instructor. She creates her own routines using old exercise tapes from a BBC fitness expert. She believes staying busy is the key to good health, especially since her husband died in 1997. She also enjoys writing poetry and has been doing so since she was 80.

The scandal began when a hotel falsely described a scallop dish, but it has grown into a larger problem for many of Japan’s best hotels and department stores. It could damage the country’s reputation for good food.

After one luxury hotel group admitted to being dishonest about the ingredients on its menus, Japanese media reported similar problems at other restaurants owned by famous hotels and stores. The Hankyu-Hanshin hotel chain in Osaka said it gave incorrect descriptions for many menu items between 2006 and 2013, affecting around 78,000 customers. 

For example, a dish described as red salmon caviar actually contained cheaper fish eggs. The hotel group’s president, Hiroshi Desaki, took a 20% pay cut, and other leaders cut their pay by 10%, but customers were still angry. Desaki later resigned, saying the hotel had “betrayed” customers, but that they didn’t mean to deceive anyone. One of the hotel’s chefs refused a government award.

The company has already given refunds of 20 million yen to over 10,000 customers, and the total cost is expected to reach 110 million yen. 

The problem has spread to other well-known companies. Like a similar scandal in the UK with horsemeat, no one has become ill from eating the wrongly labelled food, but public anger is still strong. Some customers thought they were eating expensive kuruma shrimp, but they were actually served cheaper black tiger shrimp.

Author Philip Pullman says illegally downloading music or books is a form of theft, just like stealing from someone’s wallet. He strongly defends copyright laws in an article for Index on Censorship, as he believes many people don’t understand the harm they cause by downloading content without paying.

He says people are impressed by the technology but don’t realize it’s wrong to take an artist’s work without permission. He explains that authors and musicians often struggle for years before they can earn a living from their work, and illegal downloading takes that possibility away. He believes if people enjoy something, they should pay for it.

This discussion follows a meeting between music industry leaders and British Prime Minister David Cameron about online piracy.

Cathy Casserly, from Creative Commons, has a different view. She argues that copyright laws are outdated and make it difficult for people to share and build on each other’s work. She suggests artists should find new ways to share and sell their work. She quotes writer Cory Doctorow, who says the problem isn’t piracy, but a lack of attention for artists’ work.

Index on Censorship agrees that current copyright laws don’t work well online and could unfairly punish people. They believe new ways are needed for artists to earn money.

Research by Ofcom shows a lot of illegal downloading happens. Larry Pizzi, who works in the bicycle industry, once wondered why anyone would add a motor and batteries to a bike. Some traditional bike owners feel the same way. Although electric bikes, or e-bikes, have been available since the late 1990s, bike shops haven’t always been quick to sell them, and sales in the US were initially low.

Pizzi, now CEO of Currie Technologies – the top e-bike seller in the US – believes this is changing. Other companies, like Trek, Raleigh and Specialized, also offer e-bikes and expect sales to increase. Pizzi says more companies are starting to sell e-bikes every month.

The US is different from other countries when it comes to e-bikes. In 2014, almost 32 million were sold worldwide, mostly in China, where people use them for everyday transport. E-bikes are also popular in Europe, especially in countries like the Netherlands and Switzerland. Even German postal workers and BMW offer them.

E-bikes aren’t the same as motorcycles. They are regular bicycles with an electric motor that helps you pedal. Riding one feels like cycling with a strong wind at your back. The motor helps you go faster or up hills, but you still need to pedal. E-bikes are usually allowed on bike paths and can’t go faster than 20mph.

Is streaming music becoming very popular?

In 2014, around 41 million people worldwide used music streaming services. While this is a growing area for the music industry, it was still quite small. Many of these users got their subscriptions as part of mobile phone packages, so it’s unclear how often they actually used the services. Apple has a history of making existing products, like downloads (iTunes), music players (iPod), and smartphones (iPhone), popular with a wider audience. Reports suggest Apple wants to reach 100 million subscribers, which would bring in $12 billion a year. In 2014, the entire global music industry was worth just under $15 billion. Apple is good at making products mainstream, but this would be a very large amount of money.

Is downloading music ending?

The iTunes Store started in 2003 (2004 in Europe) when illegal music sharing was a big problem. Apple convinced people to pay for downloads and became the biggest music retailer, with around 70% of the market. In 2014, downloads still made up 52% of all digital music income, and Apple earned most of this. However, download sales fell in the UK and the US in 2013 and 2014. Apple bought Beats in 2014 to move towards streaming, but they can’t stop selling downloads yet. So, Apple will offer both streaming and downloads, with streaming seen as the future.
